etymology_story.zh: 来自法语和拉丁语中表示“伸展、延长”的名词，最终与拉丁语 extendere“向外伸展”有关，其中 ex- 表示“向外”，tendere 表示“伸展”。空间上的拉长逐渐引申为时间延长、范围扩大以及附加部分。
etymology_story.en: Extension comes through French and Latin nouns meaning a stretching or lengthening, ultimately related to Latin extendere, to stretch out, from ex-, out, and tendere, to stretch. Physical lengthening developed into extra time, wider scope, and added parts.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代词族关系为 extend（延长）→ extens- + -ion → extension，词干中的 d 变为 s，不是 extend 后直接保留 d 加 -ion。词族：extend、extends、extended、extending（延长及其变化），extension、extensions（延伸及其复数），extensive（广泛的），extensively（广泛地），extensiveness（广泛性），extensible（可扩展的），extensibility（可扩展性），extensional（外延的），extensionally（从外延上），extender（延长器；扩展装置），overextend（过度扩张；使负担过重），overextension（过度扩张）。
morphology_enriched.en: The modern family relationship is extend → extens- + -ion → extension, with a d/s stem alternation rather than direct addition of -ion to unchanged extend. The family includes extend, extends, extended, extending, extension, extensions, extensive, extensively, extensiveness, extensible, extensibility, extensional, extensionally, extender, overextend, and overextension.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: expansion（扩大；扩张）强调面积、规模或数量增加；prolongation（延长）主要强调持续时间变长，语体较正式；extension（延伸；延期；扩建部分）既可指长度或期限增加，也可指新增的具体部分。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Expansion emphasizes growth in area, scale, or quantity; prolongation is more formal and mainly emphasizes longer duration; extension can refer to greater length or time as well as a specific added part.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 核心是“向外伸”：空间伸出去是扩建，时间伸出去是延期，功能伸出去是扩展。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Think of stretching outward: stretch space for an addition, time for a deadline extension, and functionality for a software extension.

usage_note: tank 可以装水、气体或其他液体；本课不是以坦克车辆的含义代替储水容器。

senses.meaning_zh: 储罐；水箱；装液体或气体的大容器
senses.meaning_en: a large container for holding liquid or gas
senses.english_definition: A tank is a large container used for storing liquid or gas.
senses.collocation_en: a fuel tank; a water tank
senses.collocation_zh: 燃油箱；储水箱
senses.sentence_en: The car's fuel tank is almost empty.
senses.sentence_zh: 这辆车的油箱几乎空了。

senses.meaning_zh: 水族箱；养鱼或其他水生动物的容器
senses.meaning_en: a container in which fish or other aquatic animals are kept
senses.english_definition: A tank is a container filled with water in which fish or other aquatic animals are kept.
senses.collocation_en: a fish tank; a tropical fish tank
senses.collocation_zh: 鱼缸；热带鱼缸
senses.sentence_en: The children watched the fish swimming around the tank.
senses.sentence_zh: 孩子们看着鱼在鱼缸里游来游去。

senses.meaning_zh: 坦克；装有履带和武器的重型装甲战斗车辆
senses.meaning_en: a heavily armoured military vehicle with tracks and weapons
senses.english_definition: A tank is a heavily armoured military vehicle that moves on tracks and usually carries a large gun.
senses.collocation_en: a battle tank; a tank crew
senses.collocation_zh: 战斗坦克；坦克乘员组
senses.sentence_en: The tank moved slowly across the muddy field.
senses.sentence_zh: 坦克缓慢地驶过泥泞的田野。

senses.meaning_zh: 无袖背心；tank top 的非正式简称，主要用于美式英语
senses.meaning_en: a sleeveless top, informally called a tank in American English
senses.english_definition: In informal American English, a tank is a sleeveless top worn on the upper part of the body.
senses.collocation_en: a cotton tank; a ribbed tank
senses.collocation_zh: 棉质无袖背心；罗纹无袖背心
senses.sentence_en: She wore a white tank with jeans.
senses.sentence_zh: 她穿着白色无袖背心和牛仔裤。

senses.meaning_zh: 坦克型角色；游戏中主要负责承受伤害、保护队友的角色
senses.meaning_en: a game character whose main role is to absorb damage and protect teammates
senses.english_definition: In some team-based games, a tank is a character whose role is to take attacks and protect other players.
senses.collocation_en: play a tank; the main tank
senses.collocation_zh: 玩坦克型角色；主坦克角色
senses.sentence_en: Our team needs a tank to protect the other players.
senses.sentence_zh: 我们队需要一个坦克型角色来保护其他玩家。

senses.meaning_zh: 暴跌；惨败；表现迅速恶化，属非正式用法
senses.meaning_en: to fall sharply, fail badly, or perform very poorly
senses.english_definition: If a price, business, or performance tanks, it falls sharply or becomes very unsuccessful.
senses.collocation_en: share prices tank; the economy tanks
senses.collocation_zh: 股价暴跌；经济急剧恶化
senses.sentence_en: The company's shares tanked after the announcement.
senses.sentence_zh: 公告发布后，这家公司的股价暴跌。

senses.meaning_zh: 故意输掉；故意表现不佳，尤用于体育比赛
senses.meaning_en: to deliberately lose or perform badly in a competition
senses.english_definition: If a player or team tanks a game, they deliberately fail to play as well as they can.
senses.collocation_en: tank a game; tank a season
senses.collocation_zh: 故意输掉一场比赛；在一个赛季中故意摆烂
senses.sentence_en: Fans accused the team of tanking games to get a better draft pick.
senses.sentence_zh: 球迷指责这支球队为获得更有利的选秀顺位而故意输球。

senses.meaning_zh: 给油箱加油；加满油，通常用于 tank up
senses.meaning_en: to fill a vehicle's tank with fuel, usually in tank up
senses.english_definition: If you tank up, or tank up a vehicle, you fill its fuel tank.
senses.collocation_en: tank up before a journey; tank up the car
senses.collocation_zh: 出发前加满油；给汽车加满油
senses.sentence_en: We tanked up before leaving the city.
senses.sentence_zh: 我们离开城市前加满了油。

senses.meaning_zh: 承担坦克角色；在游戏中承受攻击或伤害以保护队友
senses.meaning_en: to take attacks or damage for teammates in a game
senses.english_definition: If you tank in a game, you take attacks or damage so that other players are protected.
senses.collocation_en: tank damage; tank the boss
senses.collocation_zh: 承受伤害；扛住首领的攻击
senses.sentence_en: I'll tank the boss while you focus on healing.
senses.sentence_zh: 我来扛住首领的攻击，你专心治疗。

etymology_story.zh: 储水池、储液容器义经葡萄牙语 tanque 进入英语；更早来源存在争议，可能涉及印度语言，不能确定唯一的上游词源。第一次世界大战期间，tank 被用作新型装甲车辆的保密名称，后来成为“坦克”的正式通称，并进一步产生游戏中的比喻用法。
etymology_story.en: Tank entered English through Portuguese tanque in the sense of a pool or liquid container; its earlier origin is disputed and may involve Indian languages. During the First World War, tank was used as a cover name for a new armoured vehicle and became its ordinary name, later inspiring the gaming metaphor.

morphology_enriched.zh: tank 是现代英语中的单纯词，也可由名词直接转为动词；tank + -s → tanks，tank + -ed → tanked，tank + -ing → tanking，均不双写 k。词族和常用复合词：tanker（油轮；罐车；加油机），tankful（满满一箱的量；复数 tankfuls），tankless（无储水箱或储罐的），fuel tank（燃油箱），water tank（水箱），fish tank（鱼缸），tank top（无袖背心），tank up（加满油），anti-tank（反坦克的）；tankard“有柄大酒杯”不宜因拼写相似而当作 tank 的现代派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: Tank is a simple modern base and can become a verb by conversion. Its forms are tanks, tanked, and tanking, with no doubling of k. Related formations and common compounds include tanker, tankful, tankfuls, tankless, fuel tank, water tank, fish tank, tank top, tank up, and anti-tank. Tankard should not be treated as a modern derivative of tank merely because of its spelling.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 容器义中，container（容器）最宽泛，reservoir（蓄水池；储液库）强调储备和供应，tank（储罐；水箱）通常指专门储存液体或气体的容器；动词义中，plummet（暴跌）强调急剧下降，flop（失败）强调结果不成功，而 tank 可非正式地表示两者。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: For the container sense, container is the broadest term, reservoir emphasizes stored supplies, and tank usually means a purpose-built container for liquid or gas. For the informal verb, plummet emphasizes a sharp fall and flop emphasizes failure, while tank can express either.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 先记“装东西的箱体”，再联想重装甲的坦克和游戏中扛伤的角色；动词 tank 可用“表现沉到底”作记忆画面，这只是助记，不是词源。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Start with a container, then picture an armoured tank and a game character that absorbs attacks. For the failure verb, imagine performance sinking to the bottom; this is a memory image, not an etymology.

translation: 展览描述了一场改变村庄的自然灾难。
usage_note: disaster 通常带来重大损害，也可比喻糟糕结果；一件轻微不便不必就是灾难。

senses.meaning_zh: 灾难；造成重大伤亡或损失的事件
senses.meaning_en: An event causing great harm, loss, or suffering.
senses.english_definition: A disaster is a very serious event that causes people to suffer or causes a great deal of damage.
senses.collocation_en: a natural disaster; disaster relief
senses.collocation_zh: 自然灾害；救灾援助
senses.sentence_en: The earthquake was the worst natural disaster the region had experienced in decades.
senses.sentence_zh: 这场地震是该地区数十年来经历的最严重的自然灾害。

senses.meaning_zh: 惨败；彻底失败的人或事
senses.meaning_en: A complete failure or something that goes extremely badly.
senses.english_definition: If you describe something as a disaster, you mean that it fails completely or has very bad results.
senses.collocation_en: a complete disaster; a financial disaster
senses.collocation_zh: 彻底的失败；财务上的惨败
senses.sentence_en: The outdoor concert was a complete disaster because of the heavy rain.
senses.sentence_zh: 由于下起大雨，这场露天音乐会彻底搞砸了。

etymology_story.zh: 该词经法语借自意大利语 disastro，历史上由表示“不利”的 dis- 和表示“星辰”的 astro 构成，反映了把不幸归因于星象的旧观念。词义后来发展为重大灾祸，也可比喻彻底的失败。
etymology_story.en: The word entered English through French from Italian disastro, historically combining dis-, expressing an unfavorable condition, with astro, meaning 'star,' and reflecting an old belief in harmful stellar influences. Its meaning developed into a major calamity and, figuratively, a complete failure.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中以 disaster 为整体词基，不宜把它当作可自由生成的 dis- + aster；名词复数为 disaster + -s → disasters。常用派生词为 disastrous（灾难性的）和 disastrously（灾难性地）；常见复合形式有 disaster-prone（易遭灾的）和 disaster-stricken（遭灾的）。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, disaster functions as a whole base rather than a freely productive combination of dis- and aster; its plural is disaster + -s → disasters. Common derivatives are disastrous and disastrously; common compounds include disaster-prone and disaster-stricken.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: catastrophe（大灾难）通常突出破坏极其严重；calamity（灾祸）较正式，强调巨大痛苦或不幸；fiasco（惨败）指令人难堪的彻底失败，通常不指自然灾害。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Catastrophe usually emphasizes exceptionally severe destruction; calamity is more formal and stresses great suffering or misfortune; fiasco means an embarrassing complete failure and is not normally used for a natural hazard.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 历史画面：“不利的星象”→ 大祸临头 → 灾难；也可比喻事情彻底搞砸。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Historical image: 'unfavorable stars' → terrible misfortune → disaster, including something that goes completely wrong.

translation: 画稿找到时，那个角色开始松了一口气。
usage_note: sigh 可能表达疲倦、失望或宽慰；不能把每次叹气都断定为悲伤。

senses.meaning_zh: 叹气；叹息
senses.meaning_en: To breathe out slowly and audibly to express a feeling.
senses.english_definition: When you sigh, you let out a long breath that shows a feeling such as sadness, tiredness, relief, or satisfaction.
senses.collocation_en: sigh deeply; sigh with relief
senses.collocation_zh: 深深地叹气；如释重负地舒一口气
senses.sentence_en: She sighed with relief when she heard that everyone was safe.
senses.sentence_zh: 听说大家都平安无事，她如释重负地舒了一口气。

senses.meaning_zh: 叹息着说
senses.meaning_en: To say something while sighing.
senses.english_definition: If someone sighs something, they say it while letting out a long breath that expresses their feelings.
senses.collocation_en: sigh the words; sigh an apology
senses.collocation_zh: 叹息着说出那些话；叹息着道歉
senses.sentence_en: "I suppose we'll have to start again," he sighed.
senses.sentence_zh: “看来我们得重新开始了。”他叹息着说。

senses.meaning_zh: 叹气；叹息；舒出的长气
senses.meaning_en: A long, audible breath expressing a feeling.
senses.english_definition: A sigh is a long breath that you let out to express a feeling such as disappointment or relief.
senses.collocation_en: a sigh of relief; let out a sigh
senses.collocation_zh: 如释重负的一声叹息；叹一口气
senses.sentence_en: He let out a sigh and closed the unfinished report.
senses.sentence_zh: 他叹了一口气，合上了尚未完成的报告。

etymology_story.zh: 该词可追溯至古英语表示“叹息”的动词；中古英语时期，较早动词的过去时等形式影响了新的 sigh 词形。名词由动词发展而来，现代拼写中的 gh 不发音。
etymology_story.en: The word goes back to an Old English verb meaning 'to sigh'; during Middle English, forms including the older verb's past tense helped shape the newer form sigh. The noun developed from the verb, and gh is silent in the modern pronunciation.

morphology_enriched.zh: sigh 是单纯词，可作动词和名词；动词变化为 sighs、sighed、sighing，名词复数为 sighs。加 -ed 或 -ing 时保留 gh；常见派生形式 sighing 可表示“叹息的”，复合形容词 sigh-inducing 表示“令人叹气的”。
morphology_enriched.en: Sigh is a simple base used as both a verb and a noun; its verb forms are sighs, sighed, and sighing, and its noun plural is sighs. The letters gh remain before -ed and -ing; sighing can also function adjectivally, and the compound adjective sigh-inducing means 'causing someone to sigh.'

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: exhale（呼气）只说明呼出气体，不一定表达情绪；groan（呻吟；哼叹）通常声音更低沉，表达疼痛或不满；moan（呻吟；哀叹）常带有持续的痛苦或抱怨意味。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Exhale simply means to breathe out and need not express emotion; groan usually describes a deeper sound of pain or frustration; moan often suggests sustained suffering or complaint.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 一口长气带出情绪：sigh 既是“叹气”的动作，也是“一声叹息”；gh 静音。
mnemonic_anchor.en: One long breath carries a feeling: sigh names both the action and the sound; gh stays silent.

senses.meaning_zh: 惯常程序；日常安排；固定习惯
senses.meaning_en: A usual or regularly repeated way of doing things.
senses.english_definition: Your routine is the usual series of things that you do regularly.
senses.collocation_en: a daily routine; establish a routine
senses.collocation_zh: 日常安排；建立固定的生活或工作规律
senses.sentence_en: A short walk is part of my morning routine.

senses.meaning_zh: 成套表演；一套固定动作或节目
senses.meaning_en: A prepared sequence of movements, jokes, or other performance material.
senses.english_definition: A routine is a series of movements or pieces of entertainment that someone has prepared and performs together.
senses.collocation_en: a dance routine; a comedy routine
senses.collocation_zh: 一套舞蹈动作；一段喜剧表演
senses.sentence_en: The dancers practiced their routine until every movement was perfectly timed.
senses.sentence_zh: 舞者们反复练习这套动作，直到每个动作的节奏都配合得恰到好处。

senses.meaning_zh: 例程；执行特定任务的一段程序
senses.meaning_en: A section of computer code that performs a particular task.
senses.english_definition: In computing, a routine is a set of instructions that performs a particular task within a program.
senses.collocation_en: a initialization routine; an error-handling routine
senses.collocation_zh: 初始化例程；错误处理例程
senses.sentence_en: The program calls a routine that checks whether the file exists.
senses.sentence_zh: 该程序调用一个例程来检查文件是否存在。

senses.meaning_zh: 例行的；常规的；普通而缺乏变化的
senses.meaning_en: Done regularly as a normal procedure, often without much variety.
senses.english_definition: Something that is routine is done regularly as part of the normal way of doing things and may seem ordinary or repetitive.
senses.collocation_en: a routine check; routine maintenance
senses.collocation_zh: 例行检查；常规维护
senses.sentence_en: The fault was discovered during a routine inspection.
senses.sentence_zh: 这个故障是在一次例行检查中发现的。

etymology_story.zh: 该词借自法语 routine，原指沿着熟悉路径形成的惯常做法，在历史上与 route（道路；路线）相关。英语后来将它用于固定表演和计算机例程，并发展出“常规的”这一形容词用法。
etymology_story.en: The word was borrowed from French routine, referring to customary practice associated with following a familiar path, and is historically related to route. English later extended it to prepared performances and computer procedures and developed the adjective meaning 'regular or ordinary.'

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 routine 作为整体词基使用，兼作名词和形容词；复数为 routines。常用词族包括 routinely（惯常地）、routinize／routinise（使常规化）、routinization／routinisation（常规化）和 routinized／routinised（已常规化的）；加 -ly 时保留 e，加 -ize 时去掉末尾 e。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, routine is a whole base used as a noun and an adjective; its plural is routines. Its common family includes routinely, routinize/routinise, routinization/routinisation, and routinized/routinised; the final e remains before -ly but is dropped before -ize.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: habit（习惯）通常指个人反复进行的某个行为；procedure（程序；步骤）强调完成任务所规定的方法；regular（定期的；有规律的）强调重复发生，而 routine 还可突出常规性或单调感。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Habit usually means an individual behavior repeated by a person; procedure emphasizes the prescribed method for completing a task; regular stresses recurrence, while routine can additionally suggest standard practice or monotony.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 沿着同一条熟路反复走 → 固定安排、成套步骤、常规的；这是历史联系，不是现代拆词公式。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Following the same familiar path repeatedly → a fixed schedule, a prepared sequence, or something routine; this is a historical connection, not a modern word-building formula.

senses.meaning_zh: 蛋糕；糕点
senses.meaning_en: A sweet baked food, usually made with flour, sugar, eggs, and fat.
senses.english_definition: A cake is a sweet food made by baking a mixture that usually contains flour, sugar, eggs, and butter or oil.
senses.collocation_en: a birthday cake; a slice of cake

senses.meaning_en: A compact block or flat piece of a substance or prepared food.
senses.english_definition: A cake of something is a solid piece of it, and some foods shaped into small flat pieces are also called cakes.

senses.meaning_en: To cover something with a thick layer that dries or hardens.
senses.english_definition: If something is caked with mud, dirt, or another substance, a thick layer of that substance covers it.

senses.collocation_zh: 糊满厚厚的泥；沾满厚厚的污垢

etymology_story.zh: cake 在中古英语时期借自古诺尔斯语 kaka，早期可指小饼或扁圆的面包，其更早的最终来源尚不确定。词义后来扩展至甜蛋糕及各种饼状块状物，动词则由“形成块状物”的意象发展而来。
etymology_story.en: Cake was borrowed into Middle English from Old Norse kaka, which could refer to a small cake or flat loaf; its ultimate earlier origin is uncertain. It later covered sweet cakes and various compact or flat masses, with the verb developing from the idea of forming such a mass.

morphology_enriched.zh: cake 是单纯词，名词和动词同形；名词复数及动词第三人称单数为 cakes，过去式和过去分词为 caked，现在分词为 caking，后者须去掉末尾 e。常见词族有 caky／cakey（有蛋糕质感的；结块的）、caking（结块）、cake-like（像蛋糕的），以及 cupcake（纸杯蛋糕）、cheesecake（芝士蛋糕）、pancake（薄煎饼）等复合词。
morphology_enriched.en: Cake is a simple base shared by the noun and verb; cakes is the noun plural and third-person singular verb form, caked is the past tense and past participle, and caking drops the final e. Common family members include caky/cakey, caking, cake-like, and compounds such as cupcake, cheesecake, and pancake.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: pastry（酥皮糕点；油酥面团）通常强调酥皮或油酥面团；gateau（精致大蛋糕）在英式英语中常指有奶油或水果装饰的蛋糕；crust（结壳）作动词时强调形成表面硬壳，而 cake 还可表示整体结块。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Pastry usually refers to food made with pastry dough or to the dough itself; gateau, especially in British English, often means an elaborate cake with cream or fruit; crust as a verb emphasizes a hard outer layer, while cake can also mean forming solid lumps throughout.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 抓住“成形的一块”：甜的一块是蛋糕，压成的一块是饼块，泥或粉末结成一块就是 cake 的动词义。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture a formed mass: a sweet one is a cake, a compact one is a block, and mud or powder that forms a mass cakes.

senses.meaning_zh: 效率；效能；有效产出与投入的比率
senses.meaning_en: The ability to produce useful results with little waste, or the ratio of useful output to input.
senses.english_definition: Efficiency is the ability to do something well without wasting time, energy, or resources; in technical contexts, it measures useful output compared with input.
senses.collocation_en: improve efficiency; energy efficiency
senses.collocation_zh: 提高效率；能源利用效率
senses.sentence_en: Better insulation can improve the energy efficiency of a building.
senses.sentence_zh: 更好的隔热措施可以提高建筑的能源利用效率。

senses.meaning_zh: 提高效率的改进；由此实现的节约，通常用复数
senses.meaning_en: Improvements or savings achieved by using resources more effectively, usually expressed in the plural.
senses.english_definition: Efficiencies are improvements in how work is done that reduce wasted time, effort, or money.
senses.collocation_en: achieve efficiencies; operational efficiencies
senses.collocation_zh: 实现效率提升与节约；运营效率方面的改进
senses.sentence_en: Sharing equipment helped the two departments achieve significant efficiencies.
senses.sentence_zh: 共享设备帮助这两个部门显著提高了效率并节约了资源。

etymology_story.zh: 该词的历史来源与拉丁语 efficientia（产生作用的能力；效能）相连，后者属于 efficere（完成；造成）这一词族。英语中的含义由“产生效果的能力”逐渐发展为“以较少浪费取得有效产出”。
etymology_story.en: The word is historically connected with Latin efficientia, meaning effective power or productive capacity, in the family of efficere, 'to accomplish or bring about.' In English, the meaning developed from the power to produce an effect toward producing useful results with minimal waste.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代词族关系为 efficient（高效的）→ efficiency（效率），体现 -ent → -ency 的形容词转名词变化；复数为 efficiency 去 y 加 -ies → efficiencies。常用词族包括 efficiently（高效地）、inefficient（低效的）、inefficiently（低效地）、inefficiency（低效；效率低下之处）及其复数 inefficiencies；复合形式有 energy-efficient（节能的）和 cost-efficient（成本效率高的）。
morphology_enriched.en: The modern family relationship is efficient → efficiency, following the adjective-to-noun pattern -ent → -ency; the plural changes final y to -ies: efficiencies. Common family members include efficiently, inefficient, inefficiently, inefficiency, and inefficiencies, with compounds such as energy-efficient and cost-efficient.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: effectiveness（有效性）强调是否达到目标；productivity（生产率）强调单位时间或单位投入的产出；economy（节约；经济性）强调少用资源，而 efficiency 综合关注有效产出与资源投入之间的关系。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Effectiveness concerns whether a goal is achieved; productivity concerns output per unit of time or input; economy emphasizes restrained resource use, while efficiency concerns the relationship between useful results and the resources consumed.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: efficient 是“做事少浪费”，efficiency 是这种能力或比率：同样投入，得到更多有效产出。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Efficient means getting work done with little waste; efficiency names that quality or ratio: more useful output from the same input.

senses.meaning_zh: 平滑的；光滑的

senses.meaning_zh: 细腻柔滑的；口感柔和的；声音圆润的
senses.meaning_en: Pleasantly creamy, mild, or rich in texture, taste, or sound.

senses.meaning_zh: 缓和；消除困难；使进展顺利

senses.meaning_zh: 平稳地；顺畅地

senses.collocation_zh: 运转平稳；进展顺利

etymology_story.zh: smooth 源自古英语 smōþ，意为“平滑的、柔和的”，更早的来源尚不确定。其意义由表面没有凹凸，扩展为运动平稳、过程顺利以及言行圆滑。
etymology_story.en: Smooth comes from Old English smōþ, meaning smooth or gentle; its earlier origin is uncertain. The idea of a surface without roughness extended to steady movement, trouble-free processes, and polished social behavior.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代基本词为 smooth，不能可靠地再拆分；形容词与动词同形。常用词族：smooth + -ly → smoothly（平稳地、顺利地，标准副词）；smooth + -ness → smoothness（光滑、平稳）；smooth + -en → smoothen（使平滑，较少用）；smoother（更平滑的；抹平工具）、smoothest（最平滑的）；动词变化为 smooths、smoothed、smoothing。复合形式有 smooth-talking（能说会道的）和 smooth-running（运行顺畅的）；smooth 作副词主要见于非正式表达。
morphology_enriched.en: Smooth is a modern base word with no reliable smaller productive components; the adjective and verb have the same form. Common family members are smooth + -ly → smoothly, the standard adverb; smooth + -ness → smoothness; and smooth + -en → smoothen, a less common verb. Smoother is a comparative adjective or a tool noun, and smoothest is the superlative. Verb forms are smooths, smoothed, and smoothing. Compounds include smooth-talking and smooth-running; adverbial smooth is mainly informal.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: even 强调表面或分布均匀，不一定触感光滑；silky 强调丝绸般柔滑的触感或声音；suave 专指待人接物从容圆熟，常暗含刻意表现出来的魅力。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Even emphasizes uniformity of surface or distribution without necessarily implying a silky feel; silky emphasizes a soft, silk-like texture or sound; suave describes polished social confidence and may suggest deliberately cultivated charm.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 抓住“没有凸起和阻碍”：表面光滑，运动平稳，事情顺利；smooth 作动词就是把这些“凸起和阻碍”抚平。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Think 'no bumps or obstacles': a surface is even, movement is steady, and events go well; to smooth something is to remove its bumps or obstacles.

senses.meaning_zh: 部分；分得的一份

etymology_story.zh: portion 经古法语进入中古英语，源自拉丁语 portio，意为“份额、分得的一份”。“整体中分出的一份”这一核心概念形成了部分、食物份量以及分配等现代用法。
etymology_story.en: Portion entered Middle English through Old French from Latin portio, meaning a share or allotted part. The central idea of a share taken from a whole underlies its modern meanings of a part, a serving of food, and the act of dividing something into shares.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代把 portion 视为完整词基，不宜机械拆成 port + -ion；名词可零派生为动词。屈折形式为 portions、portioned、portioning；常用相关形式有 portion-sized（按一份大小的）和 portion-controlled（控制每份份量的）。apportion（分配）是相关词，进一步派生 apportionment（分配；分摊）。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, portion is a complete base and should not be mechanically split into port + -ion; the noun also functions as a verb through conversion. Inflected forms are portions, portioned, and portioning. Related formations include portion-sized and portion-controlled. Apportion is a related verb meaning to allocate shares, with the derivative apportionment.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: part 是最宽泛的“部分”，不强调分配；share 强调某人拥有、应得或承担的一份；serving 专指一次供一人食用的食物份量。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Part is the broadest term and does not imply allocation; share emphasizes an amount someone owns, receives, deserves, or contributes; serving specifically means an amount of food intended for one person on one occasion.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把整体分开，拿出其中“一份”：可以是一部分预算，也可以是一份饭；作动词就是“分份”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture one share separated from a whole: a portion of a budget or a portion of food; as a verb, portion means to divide into shares.

senses.meaning_zh: 镜子；反射镜

etymology_story.zh: mirror 经中古英语借自古法语表示“镜子”的 mireor 等形式，最终可追溯至拉丁语 mirari，意为“惊叹、赞赏地观看”。其意义由映出影像的器具，扩展为反映现实、相互对应以及复制内容。
etymology_story.en: Mirror came through Middle English from Old French forms such as mireor, ultimately tracing back to Latin mirari, meaning to wonder at or look at with admiration. Its meaning expanded from an object that reflects images to representing reality, corresponding closely, and reproducing content.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代词基为 mirror，不拆成 mirr + -or；名词零派生为动词。屈折形式为 mirrors、mirrored、mirroring；mirrored 也可作形容词，表示“带镜面的、反射的”，mirroring 可作名词，表示“模仿、镜像复制”。相关构词有 mirror + -like → mirrorlike（镜子般的）和 mirror + -less → mirrorless（无反光镜的，尤指相机）。
morphology_enriched.en: Mirror is a modern base word, not mirr + -or; the noun becomes a verb through conversion. Inflected forms are mirrors, mirrored, and mirroring. Mirrored also functions as an adjective meaning fitted with mirrors or reflective, while mirroring is a noun for imitation or digital replication. Related formations include mirror + -like → mirrorlike and mirror + -less → mirrorless, especially in reference to cameras.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: reflect 强调反射影像或表现某种状态，使用范围最广；resemble 只表示相似，不暗示复制或反映关系；replicate 强调复制相同结构、结果或内容。

senses.meaning_zh: 度假地；度假村；旅游胜地
senses.meaning_en: A place where people go for holidays and recreation.
senses.english_definition: A resort is a place where people go on holiday, often with accommodation and facilities for relaxation or sport.

senses.meaning_zh: 可求助的手段；应急办法，尤见于固定搭配
senses.meaning_en: A means of help or action used when needed.
senses.english_definition: A resort is a person, thing, or action you turn to for help, especially when other possibilities have failed.
senses.collocation_en: as a last resort; without resort to violence
senses.collocation_zh: 作为最后的办法；不诉诸暴力
senses.sentence_en: We will sell the house only as a last resort.

senses.meaning_zh: 诉诸；采取，常指不得已采用不理想的手段，与 to 连用
senses.meaning_en: To use a method, often an undesirable one, because other methods seem unavailable.
senses.english_definition: If you resort to something, you use it because you feel you have no better way to deal with a situation.
senses.collocation_en: resort to violence; resort to borrowing
senses.collocation_zh: 诉诸暴力；不得不借钱
senses.sentence_en: They resolved the dispute without resorting to legal action.
senses.sentence_zh: 他们没有诉诸法律诉讼就解决了争端。

etymology_story.zh: resort 源自古法语 resortir，含有“再出去、返回”的意思，由 re- 和 sortir 构成。英语中的“前往、求助”后来发展出“求助的办法”，而“人们经常前往的地方”则发展成今天的“度假地”。
etymology_story.en: Resort comes from Old French resortir, meaning to go out again or return, formed from re- and sortir. English senses involving going somewhere or turning for help developed into a means of assistance, while a place people regularly visited became a holiday destination.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代 resort 整体作词基，不按 re- + 英语 sort（分类）分析；表示“重新分类”的 re-sort 是另一个词。常用形式为 resorts、resorted、resorting；名词复数同为 resorts。常见搭配构式有 resort to + 名词或动名词，以及 last-resort + 名词，如 last-resort measures（最后才采用的措施）；没有广泛常用的简单后缀派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern resort is treated as a whole base, not as re- + English sort; re-sort, meaning sort again, is a separate word. Common forms are resorts, resorted, and resorting, with resorts also serving as the plural noun. Productive patterns include resort to + noun or gerund and last-resort + noun, as in last-resort measures. There are no widely used simple suffix derivatives.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: holiday destination 泛指度假目的地，不一定有配套设施；recourse 指求助的途径或可采用的办法，语体较正式；turn to 表示转而求助或采用，不像 resort to 那样常暗示不得已或手段不理想。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Holiday destination broadly means somewhere people visit on holiday and need not imply organized facilities; recourse is a formal term for an available source of help or action; turn to is more neutral than resort to, which often suggests necessity or an undesirable method.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 用“人往哪里去”串联：去休假的地方是 resort，遇到困难转去求助是 resort to。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Connect the meanings through 'where you turn': a resort is somewhere you go for a holiday; to resort to something is to turn to it when facing difficulty.

senses.meaning_zh: 提取；取出，尤指从银行账户取钱

etymology_story.zh: withdraw 形成于中古英语，由表示“离开、向后”的旧前缀 with- 与 draw（拉）组成，字面意思是“拉开、拉回”。这一空间动作后来扩展为取款、撤回言论或支持，以及退出活动等意义。
etymology_story.en: Withdraw was formed in Middle English from the old prefix with-, meaning away or back, and draw, meaning pull. The physical idea of pulling away or back expanded to taking money out, retracting statements or support, and leaving activities.

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词公式：with-（离开、向后，旧前缀）+ draw（拉）→ withdraw；这里的 with- 不表示“和……一起”。不规则变化为 withdraws、withdrew、withdrawn、withdrawing；withdraw + -al → withdrawal（撤回、退出、取款；戒断）。withdrawn 还可作形容词，表示“沉默寡言的、孤僻的”；较少见的 withdrawable 表示“可提取的、可撤回的”。
morphology_enriched.en: Formation: with-, an old prefix meaning away or back, + draw, meaning pull, → withdraw; this with- does not mean together with. Irregular forms are withdraws, withdrew, withdrawn, and withdrawing. Withdraw + -al → withdrawal, meaning removal, departure, taking money out, or symptoms following the stopping of an addictive substance. Withdrawn also functions as an adjective meaning quiet and socially reserved; the less common withdrawable means able to be taken out or retracted.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: remove 泛指把某物移走，不特别强调向后撤或退出；retract 专指正式收回言论、指控等；retreat 强调从危险、压力或对抗中后退，通常不用于取款或撤回申请。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Remove broadly means to take something away without specifically implying movement back or departure; retract specifically means to take back a statement or allegation; retreat emphasizes moving back from danger, pressure, or confrontation and is not normally used for taking out money or cancelling an application.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: with-（向后、离开）+ draw（拉）＝“拉出来、拉回去”：钱从账户取出，部队从前线撤回，申请从流程中撤回，人从活动中退出。
mnemonic_anchor.en: With- means away or back, and draw means pull: pull money out of an account, troops back from a position, an application out of a process, or yourself out of an activity.

senses.meaning_en: the property of a material or component that opposes electric current
senses.english_definition: The resistance of a material or component is a measure of how strongly it opposes the flow of electric current.
senses.collocation_en: electrical resistance; high resistance

etymology_story.zh: resistance 经古法语进入中古英语，最终源自拉丁语 resistere，意为“站住对抗”，由表示“向后、反向”的 re- 与表示“站立、停住”的 sistere 构成。它从抵抗、反对之义，扩展到物理阻力、电阻以及生物或材料的抗性。
etymology_story.en: Resistance entered Middle English through Old French and ultimately derives from Latin resistere, meaning 'stand against', formed from re-, 'back or against', and sistere, 'take a stand or stop'. Its meanings extended from opposition to physical resistance, electrical resistance, and the ability of organisms or materials to withstand something.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词可分析为 resist（抵抗）+ -ance（名词后缀）→ resistance，保留 t。主要词族：resist（抵抗）、resistant（有抵抗力的）、resistance（抵抗；阻力）、nonresistance（不抵抗）；电学相关词有 resistor（电阻器）、resistive（电阻性的）、resistivity（电阻率）；另有 resistible（可抗拒的，较少用）、irresistible（无法抗拒的）、irresistibly（无法抗拒地）和 irresistibility（不可抗拒性）。resistance 通常不可数；谈不同电阻数值或不同种类的抗性时可用 resistances。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern analysis: resist + the noun suffix -ance → resistance, retaining t. The main family includes resist, resistant, resistance, and nonresistance; electrical terms include resistor, resistive, and resistivity. Related formations include the less common resistible, plus irresistible, irresistibly, and irresistibility. Resistance is usually uncountable; resistances is possible for separate electrical resistance values or different kinds of resistance.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: opposition 强调立场或行动上的反对；resistance 强调顶住压力、变化或外力；defiance 强调公开而坚决地违抗。表示对疾病或损害的承受能力时，resilience 更强调受损后的恢复，而 resistance 强调不易受到影响。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Opposition emphasizes disagreement or action against something; resistance emphasizes withstanding pressure, change, or force; defiance emphasizes open, determined disobedience. In contexts involving harm or illness, resilience emphasizes recovery after damage, while resistance emphasizes avoiding its effects.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 抓住“站住顶回去”：人顶住压力是抵抗，物体阻碍运动是阻力，材料阻碍电流是电阻。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture something standing firm against a push: people resist pressure, objects resist movement, and materials resist electric current.

etymology_story.zh: giant 经中古英语和古法语追溯至拉丁语 gigas、gigant-，再源自希腊语 gigas、gigantos，原指神话中的巨人；传承过程中通常还涉及一个重建的通俗拉丁语形式 *gigans。这个词后来从神话中的巨大人物扩展为大个子、行业巨头及形容词“巨大的”。
etymology_story.en: Giant came through Middle English and Old French from Latin gigas, with the stem gigant-, ultimately from Greek gigas, gigantos, referring to a mythological giant; the transmission is commonly explained through a reconstructed Popular Latin form, *gigans. It later developed meanings for unusually large beings, powerful organizations, influential people, and the adjective 'very large'.

morphology_enriched.zh: giant 在现代英语中是不可再作常用词缀拆分的词基，可作名词，也可作形容词；复数 giant + -s → giants，不双写 t。词族包括 giantess（女巨人，现多见于神话或文学）、giant-sized（巨型的）；同源词有 gigantic（巨大的）、gigantically（极其巨大地）和 gigantism（巨人症；异常巨大）。gigantic 和 gigantism 使用同源的 gigant- 词干，不能简单看成直接在 giant 后添加后缀。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, giant is a base word without a useful everyday prefix-and-suffix division, and it functions as both a noun and an adjective. The plural is giant + -s → giants, with no doubling of t. Its family includes giantess, now mainly mythological or literary, and giant-sized. Related words are gigantic, gigantically, and gigantism; these use the related stem gigant-, rather than simply adding suffixes to the spelling giant.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: huge 是通用的“非常大的”；giant 常置于名词前，突出尺寸、规模或影响力；gigantic 通常语气更强，强调大得惊人。giant 还可作名词表示巨人或巨头，而 huge 和 gigantic 通常不这样使用。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Huge is a general word for very large; giant commonly appears before a noun and highlights size, scale, or influence; gigantic usually adds stronger emphasis on astonishing size. Giant also functions as a noun for an enormous being or a dominant person or organization, unlike huge and gigantic in ordinary usage.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 从“巨人”向外扩展：身体巨大是巨人，影响力巨大是巨头，放在名词前就是“巨型的”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Start with an enormous person: enormous influence makes someone a giant, and enormous size makes something a giant object.

etymology_story.zh: bid 汇合了两个古英语动词的历史：bēodan 表示“提供、宣布、命令”，biddan 表示“请求、恳求”。中古英语时期，两者的形式和部分用法逐渐交融，形成了现代的出价、吩咐和致意等用法；名词 bid 后来由动词发展而来。
etymology_story.en: Bid brings together the histories of two Old English verbs: bēodan, 'offer, announce, command', and biddan, 'ask or entreat'. Their forms and some uses merged in Middle English, contributing to the modern meanings involving offers, commands, and formal wishes; the noun developed later from the verb.

morphology_enriched.zh: bid 是单音节词基。出价、投标和叫牌义的变化为 bid–bid–bid；现在分词及动名词 bid + -ing → bidding，施事名词 bid + -er → bidder，两者都双写 d；第三人称单数和名词复数均为 bids。道别、致意义的过去式可用 bid 或 bade，过去分词通常为 bid；命令义传统变化为 bid–bade–bidden。相关词有 outbid（出价超过）、overbid（出价过高）、underbid（以更低价格投标）、biddable（顺从的；可叫牌的）和 unbidden（未经邀请的；自发出现的）。
morphology_enriched.en: Bid is a one-syllable base. For offering money, tendering, and card bidding, the forms are bid–bid–bid. Bid + -ing → bidding and bid + -er → bidder both double d; bids is the third-person singular and the plural noun. For farewell or greeting, the past tense can be bid or bade, and the past participle is usually bid; the traditional command forms are bid–bade–bidden. Related words include outbid, overbid, underbid, biddable, and unbidden.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: offer 泛指出价或提出给予，不一定有竞争；tender 强调按正式程序提交报价或投标；attempt 对应 bid 的“尝试”义，但不如 bid 常带有争取某个目标或机会的意味。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Offer is a general proposal to pay or give something and need not involve competition; tender emphasizes a formally submitted proposal or price; attempt corresponds to the effort sense of bid but less strongly suggests pursuing a particular prize, position, or opportunity.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 抓住“提出”：提出价格是出价，提出方案是投标，提出目标并争取就是一次 bid；bid farewell 则是正式地送出告别之语。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Think 'put something forward': a price becomes a bid, a proposal becomes a tender, and an effort toward a goal becomes a bid; bid farewell formally puts goodbye into words.

etymology_story.zh: naturally 在中古英语时期由 natural 加副词后缀 -ly 构成；natural 经法语源自拉丁语 naturalis，与 natura“本性、自然”及 nasci“出生”有关。由“依照自然或本性”的核心含义，它发展出天然发生、天生具备、举止不做作和“当然如此”等用法。
etymology_story.en: Naturally was formed in Middle English from natural and the adverb suffix -ly; natural came through French from Latin naturalis, related to natura, 'nature or inborn character', and nasci, 'be born'. From the idea of being in accordance with nature or character, it developed uses for natural processes, inborn qualities, unaffected behavior, and expected outcomes.

morphology_enriched.zh: natural + -ly → naturally：保留 natural 末尾的 l，再加以 l 开头的 -ly，因此写两个 l。主要词族：nature（自然；本性）、natural（自然的）、naturally（自然地）、naturalness（自然；不做作）、unnatural（不自然的）、unnaturally（不自然地）、unnaturalness（不自然）；另有 naturalist（博物学家；自然主义者）、naturalism（自然主义）、naturalistic（自然主义的；逼真的）、naturalistically（以自然主义方式）、naturalize/naturalise（使归化；使入籍）、naturalization/naturalisation（归化；入籍）、supernatural（超自然的）和 supernaturally（超自然地）。
morphology_enriched.en: Natural + -ly → naturally: keep the final l of natural and add -ly, producing ll. The main family includes nature, natural, naturally, naturalness, unnatural, unnaturally, and unnaturalness. Further related formations include naturalist, naturalism, naturalistic, naturalistically, naturalize/naturalise, naturalization/naturalisation, supernatural, and supernaturally.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: of course 对应“当然”，常用于直接确认或回应；spontaneously 强调未经计划或外部推动而自发发生；innately 强调与生俱来的特性。naturally 可覆盖预期、本性和自然过程等多个角度，具体替换取决于语境。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Of course matches the 'as expected' sense and often directly confirms or answers something; spontaneously emphasizes happening without planning or external prompting; innately emphasizes an inborn quality. Naturally covers expectations, inherent character, and natural processes, so the appropriate substitute depends on context.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: nature 是“自然、本性”：顺着自然发生、顺着本性表现，结果往往也就“自然如此”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Follow nature or someone's nature: things happen naturally, people act naturally, and expected results naturally follow.

etymology_story.zh: 名词 summary 借自中古拉丁语 summarium“摘要”，最终与拉丁语 summa“总数、总额”相关，后者源自 summus“最高的”。形容词经另一条相关路线来自拉丁语 summarius“概括的”，后来从“简略处理”发展出“快速或省去通常程序而实施”的含义。
etymology_story.en: The noun summary was borrowed from Medieval Latin summarium, 'a summary', ultimately related to Latin summa, 'total or sum', from summus, 'highest'. The adjective came by a separate related route from Latin summarius, 'concise', later developing the sense of action taken quickly or without the usual procedures.

morphology_enriched.zh: summary 在现代英语中通常作为完整词基使用，不宜机械分析为普通动词 sum + -ary。名词复数为 summary → summaries：辅音字母加 y 结尾，先把 y 改为 i，再加 -es；相关词有 summarize/summarise（概括）、summarized/summarised（已概括的）、summarizing/summarising（正在概括）、summarization/summarisation（概括；摘要生成）和 summarizer/summariser（概括者；摘要工具）。summarily 是 summary 对应的副词，通常表示“立即地、未经通常程序地”，不能普遍替代 in summary“总之”。
morphology_enriched.en: Summary normally functions as a complete base in modern English and should not be mechanically treated as the ordinary verb sum plus -ary. Its plural is summaries: change consonant + y to i and add -es. Related formations include summarize/summarise, summarized/summarised, summarizing/summarising, summarization/summarisation, and summarizer/summariser. The corresponding adverb summarily usually means 'immediately or without the usual procedures'; it is not a general replacement for in summary.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: abstract 通常指论文或学术报告前的独立摘要；synopsis 常用于故事、电影、书籍或计划的梗概；overview 强调整体鸟瞰，未必严格压缩某一原文。summary 最通用，强调提取并简述主要内容。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: An abstract is typically a self-contained summary of an academic paper or report; a synopsis commonly outlines a story, film, book, or plan; an overview presents the broad picture and need not condense one particular source. Summary is the most general term and emphasizes presenting the main points briefly.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: summary 把内容收拢成“总要点”：作名词是摘要，作形容词是概括的；程序被大幅压缩时，又有“立即、简易处理的”意思。
mnemonic_anchor.en: A summary gathers the main points into a compact whole; summary descriptions condense information, while summary actions shorten or bypass the usual procedure.

etymology_story.zh: radical 经中古英语借自晚期拉丁语 radicalis，源于拉丁语 radix，意为“根”，早期表示“属于根的、根本的”。从“触及根本”发展出“彻底改变的”和政治上的“激进的”等含义，数学中的用法也保留了“根”的概念。
etymology_story.en: Radical entered Middle English from Late Latin radicalis, derived from Latin radix, meaning “root,” and originally meant “relating to the root or foundation.” The idea of reaching the root developed into fundamental change and political radicalism, while the mathematical use also preserves the concept of a root.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中通常将 radical 视为完整词干；历史上可分析为 radic-（根）+ -al（形容词后缀）。常用词族：radically（根本地、彻底地；保留词干末尾 l，再加 -ly）、radicalism（激进主义）、radicalize/radicalise（使激进化）、radicalized/radicalised（激进化的）、radicalization/radicalisation（激进化）、deradicalize/deradicalise（使去激进化）、deradicalization/deradicalisation（去激进化）；名词复数 radicals。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, radical normally functions as a complete stem; historically, it contains radic- “root” + the adjective suffix -al. Common family members are radically (retain the stem's final l before adding -ly), radicalism, radicalize/radicalise, radicalized/radicalised, radicalization/radicalisation, deradicalize/deradicalise, and deradicalization/deradicalisation; the plural noun is radicals.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: fundamental（根本的）强调基础或本质；drastic（剧烈的、严厉的）强调措施或变化的强度；extreme（极端的）强调远离温和立场。radical 强调触及根本，在政治语境中也常指主张深刻改变现有制度。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Fundamental emphasizes foundations or essential nature; drastic emphasizes the severity of an action or change; extreme emphasizes distance from moderate positions. Radical emphasizes change at the roots and, in politics, often a desire to transform existing institutions.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 抓住“根”：改变到根上是“根本的”，主张连根改制度的人是“激进分子”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Think “root”: a radical change reaches the roots, and a political radical wants the system changed at its roots.

senses.english_definition: When you tune a radio or television to a station, you adjust it so that it receives that station.

etymology_story.zh: tune 是中古英语 tone 的一种变体，具体音形变化的原因尚不明确；它最终可追溯到希腊语 tonos，含有“拉紧、张力、音调”等意思。“曲调”义后来引申出调整乐器音高、接收频率和机器性能等动词用法。
etymology_story.en: Tune arose as a Middle English variant of tone, although the reason for the change is uncertain; its ancestry ultimately reaches Greek tonos, associated with stretching, tension, and musical pitch. The musical meaning developed into verbs for adjusting instruments, receiving frequencies, and improving mechanical performance.

morphology_enriched.zh: tune 是现代英语中的单纯词，可由名词直接转作动词。屈折形式：tunes、tuned、tuning（加 -ing 时去掉末尾 e）；派生词：tuner（调音器、调音师；调谐器）、tuneful（悦耳的，tune + -ful，保留 e）、tunefully、tunefulness、tuneless（不成调的）、tunelessly、tunelessness、untuned（未调音的）、retune（重新调音或调谐）、detune（使偏离标准音高或频率）；相关复合词有 fine-tune（微调）、fine-tuning（微调）和 autotune（自动调谐或自动校正音高）。
morphology_enriched.en: Tune is a simple modern English base that also becomes a verb by conversion. Inflections are tunes, tuned, and tuning, with final e dropped before -ing; derivatives include tuner, tuneful (tune + -ful, retaining e), tunefully, tunefulness, tuneless, tunelessly, tunelessness, untuned, retune, and detune. Related compounds include fine-tune, fine-tuning, and autotune.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: melody（旋律）与名词 tune 最接近，但更常用于音乐分析；adjust（调整）泛指改变设置或位置；calibrate（校准）强调依照标准精确调整。动词 tune 常强调使声音、接收效果或运行性能达到合适状态。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Melody is close to the noun tune but is more usual in musical analysis; adjust broadly means changing a setting or position; calibrate means adjusting precisely against a standard. The verb tune typically aims for the right sound, reception, or performance.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 从“曲调”记到“调准”：调准琴弦、调准电台、调好机器。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Start with a musical tune, then think “bring into the right setting”: tune strings, tune a radio, tune an engine.

etymology_story.zh: 表示车辆的 van 是 caravan 的缩略形式，最初用于载货的有篷车辆，后来也用于机动车和铁路车厢。caravan 最终源自表示“商旅队伍”的波斯语词；车辆义 van 并非由 vanguard 缩略而来。
etymology_story.en: The vehicle noun van is a shortening of caravan, first used for covered goods vehicles and later for motor vehicles and railway vehicles. Caravan ultimately comes from a Persian word for a traveling company of merchants; this vehicle sense of van is not shortened from vanguard.

morphology_enriched.zh: van 在现代英语中是完整的单纯词，历史上由 caravan 截短而成；复数 vans 直接加 -s，不双写 n。常用复合词包括 minivan（小型厢式客车）、camper van/campervan（宿营车）、vanload（一厢式车的载量）、van driver（厢式车司机）和 vanpool（集体乘厢式车通勤）；没有常用的独立形容词或副词派生形式。
morphology_enriched.en: Van is a complete simple base in modern English, historically formed by clipping caravan; its plural is vans, with -s added and no doubling of n. Common compounds include minivan, camper van/campervan, vanload, van driver, and vanpool; there are no common independent adjective or adverb derivatives.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: truck（卡车）是较宽泛的载货机动车名称，常指较大型车辆；minivan（小型厢式客车）通常侧重载客；lorry（英式英语中的卡车）通常指大型载货车辆。van 的典型特征是封闭的厢式车身，可用于载货或载客。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Truck is a broader term for a goods vehicle and often refers to something larger; minivan usually emphasizes passenger transport; lorry is the usual British term for a large goods vehicle. A van typically has an enclosed body for goods or passengers.

mnemonic_anchor.en: Caravan clips down to van: a shortened word for a practical enclosed vehicle.

etymology_story.zh: mutual 经中古法语 mutuel 借入英语，最终来自拉丁语 mutuus，意为“相互的、交换的”。“彼此给予”的概念发展出相互感情、共同事物以及会员共同拥有的机构等含义。
etymology_story.en: Mutual entered English through Middle French mutuel, ultimately from Latin mutuus, meaning reciprocal or exchanged. The idea of giving or sharing between people developed into reciprocal feelings, shared connections, and organizations owned by their members.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语通常把 mutual 作为完整词干，不宜把它机械拆成具有独立现代词义的 mut- 和 -ual。常用词族：mutually（相互地；mutual + -ly，保留原有 l）、mutuality（相互性）、mutualism（互利共生；互助主义）、mutualist（互助主义者；互利共生参与者）、mutualistic（互利共生的）、mutualize/mutualise（使成为互助组织；使共同分担）、mutualization/mutualisation（互助化；共同分担）、demutualize/demutualise（使互助组织转为股东制公司）、demutualization/demutualisation（互助组织股份制化）；名词复数 mutuals。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern English normally treats mutual as a complete stem rather than as independently meaningful modern parts mut- and -ual. Common family members include mutually (mutual + -ly, retaining the original l), mutuality, mutualism, mutualist, mutualistic, mutualize/mutualise, mutualization/mutualisation, demutualize/demutualise, and demutualization/demutualisation; the plural noun is mutuals.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: reciprocal（相互的）强调双向对应或回报；shared（共同拥有或经历的）强调多人共享；common（共同的）强调同为各方所有或所具有。mutual 既可表示双向关系，也可表示共同联系，如 mutual respect 和 a mutual friend。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Reciprocal emphasizes a two-way relationship or return; shared emphasizes joint possession or experience; common emphasizes something belonging or applying to several people. Mutual can describe either a two-way relationship, as in mutual respect, or a shared connection, as in a mutual friend.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 记住“两边都有”：你尊重我、我尊重你是相互；你认识他、我也认识他是共同。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Think “on both sides”: respect flowing both ways is mutual, and a friend known to both people is mutual too.

etymology_story.zh: 表示“靴子”的 boot 来自中古英语借入的古法语 bote，更早的来源尚不确定；“踢”和“赶走”等意义由靴子及用脚踢的动作引申而来。计算机中的 boot 则是 bootstrap 的缩略形式，利用了系统从初始步骤逐步自行启动的比喻。
etymology_story.en: The footwear word boot entered Middle English from Old French bote, whose earlier origin is uncertain; kicking and dismissal senses developed from footwear and the act of kicking. The computing word boot is shortened from bootstrap, using the metaphor of a system getting itself started from initial steps.

morphology_enriched.zh: boot 是现代英语中的单纯词，名词可直接转作动词；屈折形式为 boots、booted、booting，均不双写 t。常用词族及复合词包括 booted（穿靴的）、bootie/bootee（婴儿软靴或短靴）、bootlace（靴带）、bootleg（非法制作或销售；非法的）、bootlegger（非法制售者）、bootlegging（非法制售活动）、bootstrap（靴袢；自举；利用现有资源起步）、bootstrapped、bootstrapping、reboot（重新启动）、bootable（可启动的）、unbootable（无法启动的）和 bootloader（引导加载程序）。
morphology_enriched.en: Boot is a simple modern English base, and its noun can become a verb by conversion; inflections are boots, booted, and booting, without doubling t. Common family members and compounds include booted, bootie/bootee, bootlace, bootleg, bootlegger, bootlegging, bootstrap, bootstrapped, bootstrapping, reboot, bootable, unbootable, and bootloader.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: kick（踢）是最普通的动作词，boot 通常表示更用力或更随意的一踢；dismiss（解雇、免职）较正式，boot out 更口语化且突出强制离开；start up（启动）适用范围较广，boot 特别用于计算机的启动过程。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Kick is the general action word, while boot often suggests a harder or more casual kick; dismiss is more formal, while boot out is informal and emphasizes forced departure; start up applies broadly, while boot specifically describes computer startup.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 一条线记“靴子→踢→踢出去”；电脑义另记“拉起靴袢 bootstrap→启动 boot”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Follow “boot on the foot → kick → kick out”; for computers, remember “bootstrap → boot into operation.”

translation: 这个活动模型可以让访客着迷数小时。
usage_note: fascinate 在本课吸引人的兴趣；fascinated visitors 是感到着迷的人，fascinating exhibits 是令人着迷的展品。

senses.meaning_zh: 使着迷；深深吸引
senses.meaning_en: to attract and hold someone's interest strongly
senses.english_definition: If something fascinates you, it interests you so much that you want to keep watching it or learning about it.
senses.collocation_en: fascinate an audience; be fascinated by something
senses.collocation_zh: 深深吸引观众；对某事物着迷
senses.sentence_en: The way children learn languages has always fascinated me.
senses.sentence_zh: 儿童学习语言的方式一直让我着迷。

etymology_story.zh: 源自拉丁语 fascinare，原意为“施魔法、以法术迷住”，与表示“魔法、符咒”的 fascinum 有关。词义后来从魔法造成的控制转为强烈吸引人的注意和兴趣。
etymology_story.en: The word comes from Latin fascinare, meaning 'to bewitch or enchant,' related to fascinum, a spell or charm. Its meaning developed from magical influence to the powerful attraction of someone's attention and interest.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中以 fascinate 为完整词基，不宜硬拆成独立使用的词根和前缀。常见词族：fascinates（第三人称单数）；fascinated（过去式、过去分词；形容词：着迷的）；fascinating（现在分词；形容词：令人着迷的）；fascinatingly（令人着迷地）；fascination（着迷；强烈的吸引力）；fascinator（迷人者；现代也指装饰性小礼帽或头饰）。加 -ed、-ing、-ion、-or 时去掉词尾 e。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, fascinate functions as a whole base rather than a transparent combination of an independent root and prefix. Common family forms are fascinates; fascinated, the past tense, past participle, and adjective meaning deeply interested; fascinating, the present participle and adjective meaning intensely interesting; fascinatingly; fascination, meaning intense interest or attraction; and fascinator, an enchanting person or, in modern usage, a decorative headpiece. The final e is dropped before -ed, -ing, -ion, and -or.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: interest（使感兴趣）语气较普通；captivate（使倾倒、迷住）突出魅力带来的吸引；intrigue（激起好奇心）突出神秘或复杂之处。fascinate 强调兴趣强烈且持续。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Interest expresses ordinary engagement; captivate emphasizes attraction through charm; intrigue emphasizes curiosity prompted by mystery or complexity. Fascinate suggests especially strong, sustained interest.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 从“被施了魔法”到“看得入迷”：fascinate 让人着迷，fascinating 令人着迷，fascinated 感到着迷。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Think 'held under a spell': something fascinates you, the thing is fascinating, and you are fascinated.

senses.meaning_zh: 使有权；使有资格

etymology_story.zh: 经盎格鲁法语和古法语进入英语，最终来自晚期拉丁语 intitulare，意为“题名”，与 titulus（标题、称号）有关。“赋予称号”的含义进一步发展为“赋予资格或权利”。
etymology_story.en: The word entered English through Anglo-French and Old French, ultimately from Late Latin intitulare, meaning 'to give a title,' related to titulus, a title or designation. Giving someone a title also developed into granting a claim, qualification, or right.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词可分析为 en-（使具有、赋予）+ title（标题；称号；权利依据）→ entitle。常见词族：entitles（第三人称单数）；entitled（过去式、过去分词；形容词：有权享有的，或自认为理应享有特殊待遇的）；entitling（现在分词，去掉词尾 e）；entitlement（应有的权利、应得待遇；理所当然应受优待的心态，保留词尾 e）；相关词有 title、titled（有头衔的）和 untitled（无标题的）。
morphology_enriched.en: A useful modern analysis is en-, meaning to give or endow with, + title, meaning a name, designation, or basis for a right. Common family forms are entitles; entitled, the past tense, past participle, and adjective meaning having a right or expecting special treatment; entitling, which drops the final e; and entitlement, which retains the e and means a right, benefit, or expectation of special treatment. Related words include title, titled, and untitled.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: qualify（使符合资格）强调达到条件；authorize（授权）强调得到正式许可；title（给……命名）仅对应作品命名义。entitle 表示赋予权利时，强调当事人具有正当的领取或行动依据。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Qualify emphasizes meeting requirements; authorize emphasizes official permission; title matches the sense of naming a work. In its rights-related sense, entitle emphasizes having a valid claim to receive something or take an action.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: en- + title：赋予作品一个“标题”，赋予人一项“名分或权利”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: En- + title: give a work its title, or give a person a title to a right.

etymology_story.zh: 来自古英语 god，与德语 Gott 等日耳曼语同源词相对应，原本可以泛指神祇。随着基督教传播，该词也用于指唯一的上帝，现代通常以首字母大写的 God 表示；它与 good 并非同源词。
etymology_story.en: The word comes from Old English god and has Germanic relatives such as German Gott; it could originally refer to a deity generally. With the spread of Christianity, it also designated the single supreme God, now conventionally capitalized; god and good are not etymologically the same word.

morphology_enriched.zh: god 是现代英语中的单纯词。常见词族与构词：gods（复数，直接加 -s）；goddess（女神，历史形成的词形，双写 d）；godly（虔诚的）；godliness（虔诚）；ungodly（不敬神的；极其过分的）；godless（不信神的）；godlessness（不信神）；godlike（像神一样的）；godhood（神的身份）；godhead（神性、神格）；godsend（天赐之物）；demigod（半神；被极度崇拜的人）。常见复合词还有 godfather、godmother、godparent，分别表示教父、教母、教父或教母。
morphology_enriched.en: God is a simple word in modern English. Common family forms and formations include gods, with a regular plural -s; goddess, an established form with doubled d; godly; godliness; ungodly; godless; godlessness; godlike; godhood; godhead; godsend; and demigod. Common compounds also include godfather, godmother, and godparent, referring to sponsors in a child's religious upbringing.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: deity（神祇）较正式，适合宗教研究或泛称；divinity（神祇；神性）既可指神，也可指神的性质；idol（偶像）可指受崇拜的形象或人物，但不一定是真正的神。指一神教的唯一神时，God 的使用范围更特定。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Deity is a formal term for a god; divinity can mean either a deity or the quality of being divine; idol can mean a worshipped image or an intensely admired person without implying an actual deity. Capitalized God has the more specific monotheistic reference.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 小写 god 可指众神之一；大写 God 通常指信仰中的唯一神。“奉若神明”连接神祇义与偶像义。
mnemonic_anchor.en: A lowercase god may be one among many; capitalized God usually names the one supreme being. Treating someone 'like a god' connects deity with idol.

senses.meaning_zh: 广播；播送；播放
senses.meaning_en: to transmit a programme or information to a public audience
senses.english_definition: If a station or organization broadcasts a programme or event, it sends it out so that people can hear or watch it.

senses.english_definition: If you broadcast information about something, you tell it to many people, sometimes when it would be better to keep it private.

senses.sentence_en: Broadcast the seed evenly over the prepared soil.
senses.sentence_zh: 把种子均匀地撒播在整好的土壤上。

senses.meaning_zh: 广播或电视节目；播出；广播
senses.meaning_en: a programme or message transmitted to the public, or its transmission
senses.english_definition: A broadcast is a programme or message that is sent out so that a public audience can hear or watch it.

senses.collocation_zh: 现场直播；新闻广播或新闻播报

senses.meaning_zh: 广播电视的；通过广播或电视传播的

senses.english_definition: Broadcast media or material reaches the public through radio or television.

senses.meaning_zh: 以撒播方式；散撒地，主要用于农业
senses.meaning_en: by scattering over a wide area
senses.english_definition: If seed is sown broadcast, it is scattered over the ground rather than planted in rows.

senses.collocation_zh: 采用撒播方式播种；将种子散撒在地上
senses.sentence_en: The seed can be sown broadcast or planted in rows.
senses.sentence_zh: 这些种子可以撒播，也可以条播。

etymology_story.zh: 由 broad（广阔地）和 cast（投、撒）组成，最初描述向大面积土地撒播种子。后来扩展为广泛散布消息，并在无线电兴起后用于向广大受众播送节目。
etymology_story.en: Broadcast combines broad with cast and originally described scattering seed over a wide area. It later developed the sense of spreading information widely and, with radio, transmitting programmes to a large audience.

morphology_enriched.zh: broad（广阔的）+ cast（投、撒）→ broadcast，可作动词、名词、形容词和副词，其中农业副词用法较专门。词族：broadcasts（名词复数或动词第三人称单数）；broadcasting（现在分词；广播业、广播活动）；broadcaster（广播电视机构；播音员或节目主持人）；rebroadcast（重播；重播节目）；rebroadcasting（重播活动）。过去式和过去分词通常都用 broadcast，也可见 broadcasted；重播动词通常为 rebroadcast。
morphology_enriched.en: Broad + cast forms broadcast, used as a verb, noun, adjective, and adverb, with the agricultural adverb being specialized. Family forms include broadcasts, the plural noun or third-person singular verb; broadcasting, the present participle and a noun for the activity or industry; broadcaster, an organization or person that broadcasts; rebroadcast, a verb or noun; and rebroadcasting. The usual past tense and past participle are broadcast, though broadcasted also occurs; rebroadcast normally follows the same unchanged pattern.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: transmit（传输、发射）强调信号传递，不一定面向公众；air（播出）强调节目公开播放；disseminate（广泛传播）较正式，常用于信息或知识。broadcast 强调向广大受众传播；在农业语境中则对应 scatter（散撒）。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Transmit emphasizes sending a signal and need not involve a public audience; air emphasizes putting a programme before the public; disseminate is a formal term for spreading information or knowledge. Broadcast emphasizes wide distribution to an audience; in agriculture, its corresponding synonym is scatter.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: broad + cast＝向广处撒：先撒种子，再“撒”消息和节目信号。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Broad + cast means 'throw widely': first seeds, then news and programme signals.

etymology_story.zh: 承自古英语 singere，指唱歌的人，与古英语表示“唱歌”的动词 singan 有关。现代仍能直接理解为 sing 加表示行为者的后缀 -er，既可指职业歌手，也可指一般唱歌者。
etymology_story.en: Singer continues Old English singere, a person who sings, related to the verb singan, 'to sing.' It remains transparent in modern English as sing plus the agent suffix -er and can refer to either a professional or any person who sings.

morphology_enriched.zh: sing（唱歌）+ -er（做某事的人）→ singer；直接加 -er，不再加一个 g。核心词族：sing、sings、sang（过去式）、sung（过去分词）、singing（现在分词；歌唱）、singer、singers（复数）；相关派生词有 singable（适合演唱的）、unsingable（难以演唱的）和 singsong（单调起伏的声调；集体唱歌）。复合词 singer-songwriter 指创作并演唱自己歌曲的人；此处 singer 的 ng 读 /ŋ/，不另读 /ɡ/。
morphology_enriched.en: Sing + -er, the agent suffix, forms singer; no extra g is added. The core family includes sing, sings, sang, sung, singing, singer, and singers. Related formations include singable, unsingable, and singsong, meaning a monotonously rising and falling voice or an informal group singing session. The compound singer-songwriter refers to someone who writes and performs their own songs. In singer, ng represents /ŋ/, without an additional /ɡ/ sound.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: vocalist（歌手、声乐演唱者）常见于乐队或专业音乐语境；performer（表演者）范围更广，也包括演员、舞者等；songster（歌者）较文学化，也可指鸣禽。singer 是最普通、中性的称呼。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Vocalist often appears in band or professional music contexts; performer is broader and also includes actors and dancers; songster is literary and can also refer to a singing bird. Singer is the ordinary, neutral term.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: sing 是唱歌，-er 是做这件事的人：singer＝唱歌的人。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Sing is the action; -er marks the person: a singer is someone who sings.

etymology_story.zh: 借自法语 plate-forme，字面意思是“平坦的形面”，早期指平坦的台面或高台。其“提供支撑或立足之处”的概念后来扩展到政纲、公开表达的渠道以及计算机和网络平台。
etymology_story.en: Platform comes from French plate-forme, literally a “flat form,” originally referring to a level surface or raised structure. The idea of a supporting base later extended to political policies, opportunities for public expression, and computing and online services.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 platform 通常作为完整词基使用，不宜把 plat- 当作可自由使用的英语词根；名词直接转为动词。词族及常见构词：platforms（名词复数或动词第三人称单数）、platformed（过去式及过去分词）、platforming（现在分词及动名词）、platformer（平台跳跃游戏）、deplatform（取消发声平台）、deplatforming（取消发声平台的行为）、cross-platform（跨平台的）、multiplatform（多平台的）、platform-based（基于平台的）。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, platform normally functions as a complete base; plat- is not a freely usable English root. The verb is formed by conversion from the noun. Family members and common formations include platforms, platformed, platforming, platformer (a platform-jumping video game), deplatform, deplatforming, cross-platform, multiplatform, and platform-based.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: stage（舞台）强调表演或活动场所；forum（论坛、讨论平台）强调交流和讨论；medium（媒介）强调传递信息的渠道。platform 的核心是承载活动、服务或表达的基础。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Stage emphasizes a place for performance or public activity; forum emphasizes discussion and exchange; medium emphasizes a channel for communication. Platform more broadly suggests a supporting base for activities, services, or expression.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 抓住“供人站上去的台面”：人站上去演讲，观点站上去传播，软件站上去运行。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture a surface to stand on: speakers stand on it, ideas gain an audience through it, and software runs on it.

senses.english_definition: You use whenever to say that something can happen at any time or that its timing does not affect what you are saying.

senses.meaning_en: at any convenient or unspecified time, used informally

etymology_story.zh: 由 when（何时）与 ever（曾经、在任何时候）结合而来，可追溯到中古英语中的相关表达。ever 加强了时间范围，形成“每逢”或“不论在什么时候”的意思。
etymology_story.en: Whenever developed from when combined with ever, with related expressions occurring in Middle English. Ever broadens the reference to time, producing the meanings “every time” and “at any time, no matter when.”

morphology_enriched.zh: when（何时）+ ever（任何时候）→ whenever；这是固定的复合形式，没有常规屈折变化，也没有常用的直接派生词。相关构词系列包括 whatever（无论什么）、wherever（无论哪里）、whoever（无论谁）、whichever（无论哪一个）和 however（无论怎样）。
morphology_enriched.en: When + ever → whenever, a fixed compound with no regular inflections or common direct derivatives. Related formations in the same pattern include whatever, wherever, whoever, whichever, and however.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: every time（每次）突出反复发生；no matter when（无论何时）突出时间不影响结果；anytime（随时）通常较口语化，常直接表示时间。whenever 既能表达反复，也能引导表示时间不受限制的从句。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Every time emphasizes repeated occasions; no matter when emphasizes that timing makes no difference; anytime is often conversational and can directly specify an unrestricted time. Whenever covers both repetition and clauses expressing unrestricted timing.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: when 问“何时”，加上 ever 就把时间放开：每次都算，任何时候都行。
mnemonic_anchor.en: When asks about time; ever opens the range: every occasion counts, and any time is possible.

etymology_story.zh: 借自法语 appartement，源于意大利语 appartamento，与表示“分开、隔开”的 appartare 有关。最初的概念是建筑中划分出来的一套房间，后来发展为现代的公寓住宅义。
etymology_story.en: Apartment was borrowed from French appartement, from Italian appartamento, related to appartare, meaning “to separate or set apart.” The original idea was a separate suite of rooms within a building, which developed into the modern residential meaning.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语通常把 apartment 作为完整名词词基；apart（分开）+ -ment 可作理解辅助，但不是该词在英语中直接派生的历史过程。词族及常见构词：apartments（复数）、apartment building（公寓楼）、apartment block（公寓楼，尤用于英式英语）、apartment complex（公寓楼群）、apartment hotel（公寓式酒店）；apart 和 apartment 在意义及历史上相关。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern English normally treats apartment as a complete noun base. Apart + -ment can help explain its meaning, but the English word was borrowed rather than directly formed that way. Family forms and common compounds include apartments, apartment building, apartment block, apartment complex, and apartment hotel; apart is related in meaning and historical origin.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: flat（公寓住宅）主要用于英式英语，通常与 apartment 对应；condominium／condo（产权公寓）强调单套住房的独立所有权；suite（套房）强调相连的一组房间，不一定构成独立住宅。apartment 本身不说明是租住还是自有。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Flat is the usual British equivalent; condominium or condo emphasizes individual ownership of a unit; suite emphasizes a connected set of rooms that need not form an independent home. Apartment itself does not specify whether the home is rented or owned.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 联想 apart“分开”：大楼里划分出来、供一户独立生活的一套房间。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Connect it with apart: a separate set of rooms within a larger building, forming one household's home.

senses.meaning_zh: 遵循惯例的；传统的；通常的

senses.meaning_en: using ordinary military weapons rather than nuclear, biological, or chemical weapons
senses.english_definition: Conventional weapons and warfare use ordinary military equipment rather than nuclear, biological, or chemical weapons.
senses.collocation_en: conventional weapons; conventional warfare
senses.collocation_zh: 常规武器；常规战争
senses.sentence_en: The agreement limits the deployment of conventional weapons in the region.
senses.sentence_zh: 该协议限制在这一地区部署常规武器。

etymology_story.zh: 由 convention（约定、惯例）加形容词后缀 -al 构成；convention 最终源于拉丁语 convenire，意为“走到一起、达成一致”。词义由“依据约定的”发展为“遵循社会认可做法的、常规的”。
etymology_story.en: Conventional is formed from convention and the adjective suffix -al; convention ultimately comes from Latin convenire, meaning “to come together” or “agree.” Its meaning developed from “based on agreement” to “following accepted customs or standard practice.”

morphology_enriched.zh: convention（惯例、约定）+ -al（形容词后缀）→ conventional。词族包括 convention（惯例、会议）、conventionally（按惯例地）、conventionality（循规蹈矩、传统性）、conventionalize／conventionalise（使程式化或惯例化）、conventionalization／conventionalisation（程式化）、unconventional（非传统的）、unconventionally（不循常规地）、unconventionality（非传统性）；另有较少用的 conventionalism（因循守旧；约定主义）和 conventionalist（因循守旧者；约定主义者）。
morphology_enriched.en: Convention + -al, an adjective suffix, forms conventional. The family includes convention, conventionally, conventionality, conventionalize or conventionalise, conventionalization or conventionalisation, unconventional, unconventionally, and unconventionality. Less frequent derivatives include conventionalism, meaning adherence to convention or a doctrine based on conventions, and conventionalist, a person who follows or advocates such conventions.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: traditional（传统的）强调历史传承；customary（惯常的）强调某个群体或场合中习惯如此；standard（标准的、通常的）强调公认规格或普遍采用的做法。conventional 强调符合既有惯例，有时暗含缺乏新意。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Traditional emphasizes inheritance from the past; customary emphasizes habitual practice in a particular group or situation; standard emphasizes an accepted specification or usual method. Conventional stresses conformity to established practice and can suggest a lack of originality.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: convention 是“大家约定俗成的做法”；加 -al，就是“照着大家惯常做法来的”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: A convention is an accepted way of doing things; conventional means following that accepted way.

senses.meaning_zh: 个人的独立；自主；自立
senses.meaning_en: the ability or freedom to manage your life without relying on others
senses.english_definition: Independence is the ability or freedom to make your own decisions and manage your life without depending on other people.
senses.collocation_en: financial independence; gain independence
senses.collocation_zh: 经济独立；获得独立自主的能力或自由
senses.sentence_en: Having a steady income gave her greater independence.
senses.sentence_zh: 稳定的收入使她更加独立。

senses.meaning_zh: 国家或地区的独立；摆脱外部统治的状态
senses.meaning_en: freedom from political rule by another country
senses.english_definition: A country's independence is its freedom to govern itself without being ruled by another country.
senses.collocation_en: declare independence; gain independence from

senses.meaning_zh: 机构或判断不受外部控制的独立性
senses.meaning_en: freedom from outside control or improper influence
senses.english_definition: The independence of an institution or judgment is its freedom from control or improper influence by other people or organizations.
senses.collocation_en: judicial independence; editorial independence
senses.collocation_zh: 司法独立；编辑独立
senses.sentence_en: The charter protects the broadcaster's editorial independence.
senses.sentence_zh: 该章程保障这家广播机构的编辑独立性。

senses.meaning_zh: 统计学中的独立性；一个事件或变量不提供另一个的信息

senses.collocation_en: statistical independence; a test of independence

senses.sentence_en: The analysis assumes independence between the observations.

etymology_story.zh: independence 与 independent、dependence 属于同一词族；其历史词根最终关联拉丁语 dependere，字面意思是“悬挂于……之上”，后来引申为“依赖”。否定成分 in- 将这一概念转为“不依赖、不受他者支配”，并用于个人、国家及机构。
etymology_story.en: Independence belongs to the same family as independent and dependence, ultimately connected with Latin dependere, literally “to hang from,” which developed the meaning “to rely on.” The negative element in- reverses that idea, giving freedom from dependence or control for individuals, countries, and institutions.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代可分析为 in-（不）+ dependence（依赖），也可与 independent 对照理解为 -ent 变为名词形式 -ence。词族包括 depend（依赖）、dependent（依赖的；受扶养者）、dependence／dependency（依赖）、independent（独立的；独立人士）、independently（独立地）、interdependent（相互依赖的）、interdependence／interdependency（相互依赖）、interdependently（相互依赖地）；常见搭配包括 independence movement（独立运动）和 Independence Day（独立日）。
morphology_enriched.en: A modern analysis is in-, meaning “not,” + dependence; it can also be understood alongside independent through the adjective–noun alternation -ent → -ence. The family includes depend, dependent, dependence, dependency, independent, independently, interdependent, interdependence, interdependency, and interdependently. Common combinations include independence movement and Independence Day.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: autonomy（自主权、自治）强调自行决策，仍可能属于更大的组织或国家；self-reliance（自立）强调依靠自己的能力和资源；sovereignty（主权）强调国家的最高统治权。independence 广泛表示摆脱依赖或外部控制。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Autonomy emphasizes decision-making authority, possibly within a larger organization or state; self-reliance emphasizes using your own abilities and resources; sovereignty emphasizes a state's supreme governing authority. Independence broadly denotes freedom from dependence or outside control.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: depend 是“依靠”，in- 表否定：不用事事靠别人，就有 independence。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Depend means rely on; in- reverses it: independence is being able to stand and decide for yourself.

senses.meaning_zh: 使方向、顺序或趋势相反；逆转
senses.meaning_en: to change a direction, order, or trend to its opposite
senses.english_definition: If you reverse a direction, order, or trend, you change it so that it becomes the opposite of what it was.
senses.collocation_en: reverse the order; reverse a trend
senses.collocation_zh: 颠倒顺序；逆转趋势
senses.sentence_en: To display the newest messages first, reverse the order of the list.
senses.sentence_zh: 要先显示最新的消息，请将列表顺序颠倒。

senses.meaning_zh: 撤销或推翻决定、判决等
senses.meaning_en: to cancel or overturn a previous decision or judgment
senses.english_definition: If someone reverses a decision or judgment, they change it or decide that it no longer applies.
senses.collocation_en: reverse a decision; reverse a ruling
senses.collocation_zh: 撤销决定；推翻裁决
senses.sentence_en: The appeal court reversed the original ruling.
senses.sentence_zh: 上诉法院推翻了原裁决。

senses.meaning_zh: 倒车；使车辆后退
senses.meaning_en: to move a vehicle backwards
senses.english_definition: When you reverse or reverse a vehicle, you drive it backwards.
senses.collocation_en: reverse into a parking space; reverse out of a driveway
senses.collocation_zh: 倒车进入停车位；从车道倒车出来
senses.sentence_en: She reversed carefully into the parking space.
senses.sentence_zh: 她小心地倒车进入停车位。

senses.meaning_zh: 相反的；反向的；背面的
senses.meaning_en: opposite in direction or order, or relating to the back of something
senses.english_definition: The reverse direction or order is the opposite one, and the reverse side of something is its back.
senses.collocation_en: reverse order; the reverse side
senses.collocation_zh: 相反的顺序；背面
senses.sentence_en: Write your address on the reverse side of the form.
senses.sentence_zh: 请在表格背面填写你的地址。

senses.meaning_zh: 相反的情况；反面
senses.meaning_en: the opposite of something
senses.english_definition: The reverse of something is its opposite.
senses.collocation_en: quite the reverse; the reverse is true
senses.collocation_zh: 恰恰相反；实际情况正好相反
senses.sentence_en: I expected the journey to be relaxing, but it was quite the reverse.
senses.sentence_zh: 我原以为这趟旅程会很轻松，实际却恰恰相反。

senses.meaning_zh: 物体的背面；硬币的反面
senses.meaning_en: the back of an object, especially a coin or document
senses.english_definition: The reverse of an object is the side opposite its front or main side.
senses.collocation_en: on the reverse; the reverse of a coin
senses.collocation_zh: 在背面；硬币的反面
senses.sentence_en: The date is printed on the reverse of the photograph.
senses.sentence_zh: 日期印在照片背面。

senses.meaning_zh: 倒挡
senses.meaning_en: the gear that makes a vehicle move backwards
senses.english_definition: Reverse is the gear you use when you want a vehicle to move backwards.
senses.collocation_en: in reverse; put the car into reverse
senses.collocation_zh: 处于倒挡；把汽车挂入倒挡
senses.sentence_en: He put the car into reverse and checked the mirrors.
senses.sentence_zh: 他把汽车挂入倒挡，查看了一下后视镜。

senses.meaning_zh: 挫折；失败，尤用于正式语境
senses.meaning_en: a setback or defeat, especially in formal usage
senses.english_definition: A reverse is a failure or defeat that makes progress more difficult.
senses.collocation_en: suffer a reverse; a financial reverse
senses.collocation_zh: 遭受挫折；财务上的挫折
senses.sentence_en: The party suffered a major reverse in the election.
senses.sentence_zh: 该党在选举中遭受了重大挫败。

etymology_story.zh: 形容词和名词经古法语 revers 等形式进入英语，最终源自拉丁语 reversus，意为“转回的”，与 revertere“返回、转回”有关。动词经盎格鲁法语及古法语 reverser 等形式传入，后来发展出颠倒顺序、推翻决定和倒车等意义。
etymology_story.en: The adjective and noun entered English through Old French forms such as revers, ultimately from Latin reversus, meaning 'turned back,' associated with revertere, 'to return or turn back.' The verb came through Anglo-French and Old French forms such as reverser and developed meanings involving opposite order, overturned decisions, and backward movement.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语通常把 reverse 视为完整词基；历史上的 re- 表示“回、向后”，vers- 与“转”有关，但不能把它解释成现代 re- 加普通名词 verse。屈折形式：reverses、reversed、reversing；派生词族：reverse 去 e + -al → reversal（逆转、撤销），reversible（可逆的）、reversibly（可逆地）、reversibility（可逆性），以及 irreversible（不可逆的）、irreversibly（不可逆地）、irreversibility（不可逆性）。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, reverse is normally treated as a whole base; historically, re- means 'back' and vers- relates to turning, but the word is not formed from modern re- plus the ordinary noun verse. Inflections are reverses, reversed, and reversing; derivatives include reverse minus final e plus -al → reversal, reversible, reversibly, reversibility, and the negative forms irreversible, irreversibly, and irreversibility.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: invert 强调上下、内外或排列位置的颠倒；overturn 强调推翻既有决定或判决；undo 强调消除先前行为的结果。reverse 的范围更广，还能表示趋势转向和车辆后退。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Invert emphasizes turning something upside down, inside out, or into an opposite arrangement; overturn emphasizes rejecting an established decision or judgment; undo emphasizes removing the effects of an earlier action. Reverse has a wider range and also covers changing trends and moving vehicles backwards.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 历史词根逻辑是“向后转”：方向转回去、顺序倒过来、决定翻回去。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Use the historical idea 'turn back': turn a direction back, turn an order around, or turn a decision over.

senses.meaning_zh: 插图；说明性图片或图表
senses.meaning_en: a picture or diagram that accompanies or explains a text
senses.english_definition: An illustration is a picture or diagram in a book, article, or other text that helps explain or decorate it.
senses.collocation_en: a full-page illustration; colour illustrations
senses.collocation_zh: 整页插图；彩色插图
senses.sentence_en: The book includes clear illustrations of the human skeleton.
senses.sentence_zh: 这本书配有清晰的人体骨骼插图。

senses.meaning_zh: 说明某事的实例；例证
senses.meaning_en: an example that explains or demonstrates something
senses.english_definition: An illustration of something is an example that helps you understand it or shows that it is true.
senses.collocation_en: a clear illustration of; by way of illustration
senses.collocation_zh: ……的明确例证；作为说明
senses.sentence_en: This case provides a clear illustration of the problem.
senses.sentence_zh: 这个案例清楚地说明了这一问题。

senses.meaning_zh: 插画创作；用图片说明的活动或技艺
senses.meaning_en: the activity or art of producing explanatory or decorative pictures
senses.english_definition: Illustration is the activity or art of creating pictures for books, advertisements, and other materials.
senses.collocation_en: book illustration; scientific illustration
senses.collocation_zh: 书籍插画创作；科学插画
senses.sentence_en: She studied illustration before becoming a children's book artist.
senses.sentence_zh: 她先学习了插画，后来成为儿童图书画家。

etymology_story.zh: illustration 经法语进入英语，最终来自拉丁语 illustratio，与 illustrare“照亮、阐明”有关。其“使事物清楚”的意义后来延伸为说明性实例，也发展出图画和插图的意义。
etymology_story.en: Illustration entered English through French and ultimately comes from Latin illustratio, related to illustrare, 'to illuminate or make clear.' The idea of making something clear developed into explanatory examples and, later, explanatory pictures.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词对应：illustrate（说明、加插图）去词尾 e + -ion → illustration；也可概括为 -ate → -ation 的名词化模式。常用词族：illustrates、illustrated、illustrating（动词形式），illustrations（名词复数），illustrator（插画家）、illustrators（复数），illustrative（说明性的）、illustratively（以说明方式）；历史上的词根结构不宜当作现代可自由拆分的普通词素。
morphology_enriched.en: The modern word-building relationship is illustrate minus final e plus -ion → illustration, also describable as the -ate → -ation noun pattern. Common family forms include illustrates, illustrated, illustrating, illustrations, illustrator, illustrators, illustrative, and illustratively; the deeper historical structure should not be treated as freely productive modern English components.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: picture 泛指图画或照片，不一定承担说明功能；diagram 指突出结构、关系或过程的示意图；example 指例子，不必是视觉材料。illustration 可以指配文图片，也可以指帮助理解的例证。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Picture is a broad term for an image and need not imply an explanatory purpose; diagram emphasizes structure, relationships, or processes; example need not be visual. Illustration can mean either an accompanying image or an example that makes an idea clearer.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 抓住“照亮理解”：用图把内容照亮，用例子把道理讲清。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Think 'light up understanding': a picture makes the text clearer, and an example makes the idea clearer.
