etymology_story.zh: six 源自古英语 six、siex 等形式，是继承自早期日耳曼语的数词，与德语 sechs 同源。其基本数量义保持稳定，后来也用于数字符号、六个一组和板球六分击球等名词意义。
etymology_story.en: Six comes from Old English forms including six and siex and is an inherited Germanic numeral related to German sechs. Its basic numerical meaning has remained stable, with noun uses developing for the written figure, groups of six, and six-run boundary shots in cricket.

morphology_enriched.zh: six 是现代英语中不可再分的数词词基，用于名词时构成 six + -es → sixes。主要词族有 sixth（第六；六分之一）、sixthly（第六点）、sixteen（十六）、sixteenth（第十六）、sixty（六十）、sixties（六十几；六十年代）、sixtieth（第六十）、sixfold（六倍的；六重地）、sixer（板球六分击球等），以及 six-pack（六件装；六块腹肌）、six-sided（六面的或六边的）、six-legged（六条腿的）、six-shooter（六发左轮手枪）等复合词。
morphology_enriched.en: Six is an indivisible numeral base in modern English; its noun plural is six + -es → sixes. Its principal word family includes sixth, sixthly, sixteen, sixteenth, sixty, sixties, sixtieth, sixfold, and sixer. Compounds include six-pack, meaning a pack of six or visibly defined abdominal muscles, six-sided, six-legged, and six-shooter, a six-shot revolver.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 精确数词 six 没有可普遍替换的普通近义词。half a dozen 表示同样的数量，日常交谈中很常见；sextet 指六人或六物的组合，尤常用于音乐；sixer 在板球语境中可指一次六分击球，不能代替所有用法中的 six。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: The exact numeral six has no ordinary synonym that works in every context. Half a dozen expresses the same quantity and is common in conversation; a sextet is a group of six, especially musicians; a sixer can mean a six-run shot in cricket but cannot replace six in every use.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 想象普通骰子的六点面：six 表示“六”，roll a six 就是“掷出六点”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture the six-dot face of a standard die: six names the quantity, and roll a six means land on that face.

etymology_story.zh: best 源自古英语 betst，是与 better 的古英语形式相关的最高级形式，历史上并非由 good 加后缀构成。它后来也用于表示“最佳表现、最好的人或事物”，并发展出“击败、胜过”的动词义。
etymology_story.en: Best comes from Old English betst, a superlative historically related to the forms behind better rather than formed by adding a suffix to good. It also developed noun uses for the finest performance, people, or things, and a verb meaning to defeat or surpass.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代比较体系：good（好的）→ better（更好的）→ best（最好的）；well（好地）→ better（更好地）→ best（最好地），属于异干比较，不能把 best 机械拆成现代词根与后缀。名词复数及动词第三人称单数为 bests；动词变化为 best—bested—bested，进行式为 besting。常见相关复合词：best-known（最知名的）、best-selling（畅销的）、bestseller／best-seller（畅销书或畅销商品）、best-ever（有史以来最好的）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern comparison patterns: good → better → best and well → better → best. These are suppletive forms, so best has no productive modern root-plus-suffix breakdown. Bests is the plural noun or third-person singular verb; the other verb forms are bested and besting. Common related compounds include best-known, meaning most widely known; best-selling, meaning selling in very large numbers; bestseller or best-seller, meaning a highly successful book or product; and best-ever, meaning the finest achieved at any time.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: finest（最优秀的）强调品质或技艺出众；optimal（最优的）强调在特定条件下最合适或最有效；outdo（胜过）对应动词 best，强调表现超过对方，不一定涉及直接比赛。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Finest emphasizes exceptional quality or skill; optimal emphasizes suitability or effectiveness under particular conditions; outdo corresponds to the verb best and emphasizes superior performance without necessarily involving a direct contest.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把 good／well → better → best 看成三级台阶：到顶就是“最好”；动词 best 就是“表现压过对方”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture three steps: good or well → better → best. The top step is the finest level; to best someone is to perform above them.

etymology_story.zh: better 源自古英语 betera，属于表示“更好”的古老日耳曼语比较级形式，并不是由现代英语 good 加 -er 构成。它由比较意义进一步发展出“改善”和“超过已有成绩”的动词义。
etymology_story.en: Better comes from Old English betera, an inherited Germanic comparative meaning more good, rather than from modern English good plus -er. Its comparative meaning also gave rise to verbs meaning to improve something and to exceed an existing achievement.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代比较体系：good（好的）／well（好地；健康的）→ better（更好的；更好地；身体好些的）→ best（最好的；最好地），属于异干比较；better 不宜按现代构词法拆成独立词根加 -er。动词：better—bettered—bettered，进行式 bettering，第三人称单数 betters；名词复数 betters。派生词：better + -ment → betterment（改善）；常见相关形式：better-off（境况更好的，作定语时加连字符）、better-known（更知名的）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern comparison patterns: good or well → better → best. This is suppletion; better should not be analyzed as an independent modern root plus productive -er. Verb forms are better, betters, bettered, and bettering; the plural noun is betters. The derivative betterment consists of better + -ment and means improvement. Related forms include better-off, meaning in more favorable circumstances and hyphenated before a noun, and better-known, meaning more widely known.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: superior（更优的）强调质量、能力或等级更高，通常接 to；improve（改善）与动词 better 接近，但既可及物也可不及物；surpass（超过）对应“胜过、超过成绩”的 better，强调超出某人或某一标准。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Superior emphasizes higher quality, ability, or rank and usually takes to; improve resembles the improvement sense of better but can be transitive or intransitive; surpass matches the achievement sense and emphasizes exceeding a person or standard.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: better 的核心是“比原来或别人高一级”：事物更好、做得更好、身体好转，也能主动改善或超越。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Better means one level above a comparison point: higher quality, improved performance, better health, or an action that improves or exceeds something.

etymology_story.zh: eight 源自古英语 eahta，经日耳曼语传承而来，与拉丁语 octo 和希腊语 oktō 同源，并非借自这两种语言。其核心数值意义一直是“八”，后来也用作表示数字符号、纸牌和八人赛艇的名词。
etymology_story.en: Eight comes from Old English eahta through Germanic inheritance and is cognate with Latin octo and Greek oktō, rather than borrowed from either language. Its numerical meaning has remained eight, with noun uses extending to the numeral, playing cards, and rowing boats or crews.

morphology_enriched.zh: eight 是现代英语中不可再作有意义拆分的数词词基。主要词族：eight + -s → eights（多个数字8、八点纸牌或八人艇等）；eight + 序数后缀 -th → eighth（第八，规范拼写只有一个 t）；eight + -fold → eightfold（八倍的；八倍地）。相关数词：eighteen（十八）、eighteenth（第十八）、eighty（八十）、eightieth（第八十）、eighties（八十多岁；八十年代）；复合词如 eight-sided（八边的）。
morphology_enriched.en: Eight is a simple numeral base with no meaningful internal division in modern English. Principal family members are eights, the plural noun; eighth, the ordinal formed with -th and spelled with only one t; and eightfold, meaning eight times as much or eight times over. Related numerals are eighteen, eighteenth, eighty, and eightieth. Eighties refers to ages or years from eighty through eighty-nine; eight-sided means having eight sides.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 8 是 eight 的阿拉伯数字写法，数值完全相同；a group of eight（八个组成的一组）强调成组数量；octet（八人组或八件套）是较专门的名词，常用于音乐等领域，不能在所有位置替换 eight。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: 8 is the Arabic numeral for eight and has exactly the same numerical value; a group of eight emphasizes a collection of that size; octet is a more specialized noun for a group of eight, especially in music, and cannot replace eight in every context.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 想象蜘蛛的八条腿：eight 表示“八”，eighth 表示排到“第八”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture a spider's eight legs: eight tells you how many, while eighth tells you the position.

etymology_story.zh: million 经法语进入英语，源自意大利语 milione，后者由表示“千”的 mille 加上增大后缀构成，原有“大千”之意。它后来固定表示一千个一千，也常被夸张地用来表示极多。
etymology_story.en: Million entered English through French from Italian milione, formed from mille, meaning 'thousand,' with an augmentative suffix suggesting a 'great thousand.' It came to denote a thousand thousand and also developed an emphatic use meaning a very large number.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 million 是整体数词，不宜按英语词根和后缀硬拆。million + -s → millions（数百万；极多）；million + -th → millionth（第一百万；百万分之一）；million + -aire → millionaire（百万富翁）；multi- + millionaire → multimillionaire（拥有数百万以上财富的人）；multi- + million → multimillion（数百万的，常用于复合修饰语）；million + -fold → millionfold（一百万倍的／地）。明确数词后通常不用复数：two million；表示不定数量用 millions of。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, million is a whole numeral rather than a transparent English root-plus-affix formation. Its family includes millions (plural quantities or a very large number), millionth (the ordinal or one part in a million), millionaire (a person worth at least a million monetary units), multimillionaire (a person worth several million or more), multimillion (involving several million, often in compound modifiers), and millionfold (a million times as much). Use the singular form after a specific number, as in two million, but millions of for an indefinite quantity.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: a thousand thousand（千个一千）是精确的数值释义；a great many（许多）只对应夸张用法，不表示确切数值；countless（数不清的）强调数量多到难以计数。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: A thousand thousand is an exact numerical paraphrase. A great many matches only the emphatic use, without specifying a number. Countless emphasizes that the quantity is too large to count easily.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 历史上的“大千”：一千 × 一千 = 一百万；millions 再延伸为“多得惊人”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Think of the historical 'great thousand': 1,000 × 1,000 = a million; millions can then suggest an astonishingly large number.

etymology_story.zh: twenty 源自古英语 twentig，其中前一部分与“二”有关，后一部分表示“十的组数”。“两组十”的数值意义保留至今，复数形式后来也用于年龄段和年代。
etymology_story.en: Twenty comes from Old English twentig, combining an element related to 'two' with an element meaning groups of ten. Its meaning of 'two tens' survives today, while the plural also came to name an age range or a decade.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 twenty 是整体数词，历史上的 -ty 表示“几十”，并不是可任意使用的现代派生后缀。twenty 的复数将 y 改为 ies，得到 twenties（二十多岁；二十年代；多张二十元面额钞票）；序数词为 twentieth（第二十），也可表示“二十分之一”。常见复合形式有 twenty-one 至 twenty-nine（二十一至二十九）、twenty-first（第二十一）、twenty-something（二十多岁的人；二十多岁的）及 twentyfold（二十倍的／地）。
morphology_enriched.en: Twenty is a whole numeral in modern English; its historical ending -ty marks tens but is not a freely productive modern derivational suffix. The plural changes y to ies: twenties, used for an age range, a decade, or several twenty-unit banknotes. The ordinal and fractional form is twentieth. Common compounds include twenty-one through twenty-nine, twenty-first, twenty-something (a person in their twenties, or describing such a person), and twentyfold (twenty times as much).

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: two tens（两组十）是精确的数值释义；a score（二十个）也表示二十，但在一般计数中较传统或文学化；a twenty-unit note（二十元面额钞票）只对应钞票义，具体币种由语境决定。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Two tens is an exact numerical paraphrase. A score also means twenty, but sounds traditional or literary in ordinary counting. A twenty-unit note matches only the banknote sense, with the currency supplied by context.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: two 的历史亲属 + “十组”成分：两组十就是 twenty；twenties 则是一段以二十开头的年龄或年份。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Connect its historical 'two' element with groups of ten: two tens make twenty; twenties groups together ages or years beginning with twenty.

etymology_story.zh: hundred 来自古英语 hundred，是日耳曼语族继承下来的古老数词。其现代标准数值为一百，复数 hundreds 也发展出“数百；许多”的不定数量用法。
etymology_story.en: Hundred comes from Old English hundred, an inherited Germanic number word. Its standard modern value is one hundred, while the plural hundreds also developed an indefinite use meaning several hundred or simply a large number.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 hundred 是整体词，不拆成可独立使用的现代词根和后缀。hundred + -s → hundreds（数百；多个百）；hundred + -th → hundredth（第一百；百分之一）；hundred + -fold → hundredfold（一百倍的／地）。常见复合词有 hundredweight（英美制传统重量单位）和 hundred-year（一百年的，用于名词前）。明确数词后用 hundred，如 three hundred；不定数量用 hundreds of。
morphology_enriched.en: Hundred is a whole word in modern English, without a transparent breakdown into independently usable modern roots and affixes. Its family includes hundreds (plural quantities), hundredth (the ordinal or one part in a hundred), and hundredfold (a hundred times as much). Common compounds include hundredweight, a traditional British and American weight unit, and hundred-year, used before a noun. Use hundred after a specific number, as in three hundred, and hundreds of for an indefinite quantity.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: ten tens（十组十）是精确的数值释义；a century（一个世纪）表示一百年，也在板球中表示一百分，不能普遍替换 hundred；hundreds of 与 a great many（许多）在不定数量语境中接近，但前者通常暗示数百的量级。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Ten tens is an exact numerical paraphrase. A century means a hundred years, or a hundred runs in cricket, so it cannot replace hundred generally. Hundreds of can resemble a great many, but usually suggests a quantity on the scale of several hundred.

mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture ten rows of ten: 10 × 10 makes a hundred; hundreds of means quantities counted in hundreds.

etymology_story.zh: ten 源自古英语 tīen 等形式，属于日耳曼语族继承的数词，与德语 zehn 同源。它一直表示“十”，后来也自然用于十元面额的钞票和十分的评分。
etymology_story.en: Ten comes from Old English forms including tīen and is an inherited Germanic numeral related to German zehn. Its numerical meaning remained stable, with later applications to ten-unit banknotes and scores of ten points.

morphology_enriched.zh: ten 是不可再拆的现代基本数词。ten + -s → tens（多个十；十位）；ten + -th → tenth（第十；十分之一）；ten + -fold → tenfold（十倍的／地）；ten + -ner → tenner（十英镑钞票，英国非正式用语）。常见复合形式有 ten-year-old（十岁的；十岁的人）、ten-point（十点的；十分制的）及 ten-sided（十边的）。teen 和 -teen（十三至十九中的构词成分）与 ten 有历史联系，teenage（青少年的）、teenager（十三至十九岁的青少年）属于其相关词族。
morphology_enriched.en: Ten is a basic modern numeral with no smaller meaningful parts. Its family includes tens (plural groups of ten or the tens place), tenth (the ordinal or one part in ten), tenfold (ten times as much), and tenner (an informal British word for a ten-pound note). Common compounds include ten-year-old, ten-point, and ten-sided. Teen and the ending -teen in thirteen through nineteen are historically related to ten; teenage and teenager belong to this related family.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: two fives（两组五）是精确的数值释义；a tenner（十英镑钞票）只对应英国非正式钞票义；full marks（满分）只在十分为最高分时与 a ten 对应，因为满分也可能是一百等其他分值。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Two fives is an exact numerical paraphrase. A tenner matches the banknote sense specifically in informal British usage. Full marks matches a ten only when ten is the maximum, since other scoring systems have different totals.

mnemonic_anchor.en: Hold up both hands: ten fingers make ten; on a ten-point scale, a ten means every point is present.

etymology_story.zh: Mrs 最初是 mistress 的书面缩写；mistress 曾可作为对女性的尊称，并不始终限定婚姻状况。后来 Mrs 逐渐专用于通常已婚的女性，其读音也演变成今天的 /ˈmɪsɪz/。
etymology_story.en: Mrs began as a written abbreviation of mistress, which once served as a respectful title for women without consistently specifying marital status. Mrs later became associated mainly with married women and developed its present pronunciation, /ˈmɪsɪz/.

morphology_enriched.zh: Mrs 是 mistress 的历史缩写，不由现代英语词根加后缀构成，也不是 Mr 加复数 -s。常见拼写为 Mrs（英式英语通常不加句点）和 Mrs.（美式英语通常加句点），首字母大写；它没有常用的生产性派生词族。相关称谓有 Mr（先生）、Miss（小姐，通常用于未婚女性）和 Ms（女士，不表明婚姻状况）；这些是并列称谓，不是 Mrs 的派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: Mrs is a historical abbreviation of mistress, not a modern root-plus-suffix formation and not Mr plus a plural -s. It is normally written Mrs in British English and Mrs. in American English, with an initial capital, and has no common productive family of derivatives. Related titles are Mr, Miss, and Ms; these are parallel titles rather than derivatives of Mrs.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: Ms（女士）不表明婚姻状况；Miss（小姐）通常用于未婚女性或女孩；madam（女士；夫人）通常是独立的正式称呼，不像 Mrs 那样常规地置于姓氏前。称呼具体的人时，应采用对方使用的称谓。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Ms does not specify marital status. Miss usually refers to an unmarried woman or a girl. Madam is generally a formal form of direct address rather than a title routinely placed before a surname as Mrs is. Use the title the individual uses.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 记成一个整体：Mrs Smith＝史密斯太太；拼写保留 mistress 的历史痕迹，读作 /ˈmɪsɪz/。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Learn it as a complete title: Mrs Smith means the woman addressed as Mrs Smith; the spelling preserves its link to mistress, but the pronunciation is /ˈmɪsɪz/.

etymology_story.zh: lord 源自古英语 hlāford，是 hlāfweard 的缩略形式；其中 hlāf 意为“面包”，weard 意为“守护者”。“面包的守护者”由供养和管理一家之人，逐渐发展为主人、领主、贵族及对上帝的尊称。
etymology_story.en: Lord comes from Old English hlāford, a shortened form of hlāfweard, combining words meaning “loaf” and “guardian.” The household provider and guardian developed into the master of an estate, a nobleman, and a religious title for God.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 lord 是不可再按常用词缀拆分的词根词；历史上的“面包＋守护者”不属于现代构词。常用词族：lord → lords（名词复数或动词第三人称单数）、lorded（过去式及过去分词）、lording（现在分词）；lord + -ship → lordship（贵族身份、领主权；尊称）；lord + -ly → lordly（贵族般的；傲慢的）→ lordliness（威严；傲慢）；over- + lord → overlord（最高领主；支配者）→ overlordship（最高统治权）；land + lord → landlord（房东；地主）。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, lord is a simple base; its historical “loaf + guardian” structure is no longer a productive analysis. Its common family includes lords, lorded, and lording; lord + -ship → lordship, meaning noble status, authority, or a form of address; lord + -ly → lordly → lordliness; over- + lord → overlord → overlordship; and land + lord → landlord, meaning a property owner who rents property to others.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: nobleman（男性贵族）泛指贵族身份，lord 还可直接用作头衔；master（主人；支配者）侧重控制关系，不必具有贵族身份；dominate（支配）是较中性的动词，而 lord it over 明显含有摆架子、欺压人的贬义。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Nobleman broadly identifies a man of noble rank, whereas lord can also function as a title. Master emphasizes control or authority without necessarily implying nobility. Dominate is relatively neutral, while lord it over specifically suggests arrogant or unpleasant superiority.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 历史锚点：“守护面包的人”掌管家业，进而成为“主人、领主”；像领主一样压人，就是 lord it over。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Historical anchor: the guardian of the bread controls the household and becomes its lord; acting arrogantly like a ruler gives lord it over.

etymology_story.zh: owned 是 own 的规则屈折形式；动词 own 源自古英语 āgnian，与表示“自己的”的 āgen 及表示“拥有”的 āgan 同源。“拥有”后来引申为认领责任或身份，并在非正式用法中发展出“完全掌控、彻底击败”的意思。
etymology_story.en: Owned is a regular inflected form of own, whose verbal ancestry includes Old English āgnian, related to āgen, meaning “one's own,” and āgan, meaning “possess.” Possession later extended to accepting responsibility or identity, and informally to dominating or decisively defeating someone.

morphology_enriched.zh: own + -ed → owned，其中 -ed 是屈折后缀，既可标记过去式，也可构成过去分词，并不一律表示“曾经拥有、现在不再拥有”；own 以 /n/ 结尾，因此 -ed 读 /d/。常用词族：own、owns、owned、owning；own + -er → owner（所有者）；owner + -ship → ownership（所有权）；co-own（共同拥有）、co-owner（共同所有者）、co-ownership（共同所有权）；常见复合形容词有 privately owned（私有的）、state-owned（国有的）、family-owned（家族所有的）、employee-owned（员工持有的）和 pre-owned（二手的）。own up 表示“坦白承认”，是短语动词。
morphology_enriched.en: Own + -ed → owned: -ed is an inflection marking either the past tense or the past participle, so owned does not necessarily mean that ownership has ended. After /n/, -ed is pronounced /d/. The common family includes own, owns, owned, owning, owner, ownership, co-own, co-owner, and co-ownership. Common adjectival combinations include privately owned, state-owned, family-owned, employee-owned, and pre-owned, meaning previously owned or second-hand. Own up is a phrasal verb meaning to admit something.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: possessed（拥有）侧重持有或具有，未必强调法律产权；belonged to（属于）从物的角度说明归属，而 owned 通常以所有者作主语；dominated（支配；占绝对优势）对应 owned 的非正式引申义，但本身不一定表示让对方出丑。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Possessed emphasizes having something and need not establish legal title. Belonged to describes ownership from the thing's perspective, whereas owned usually takes the owner as its subject. Dominated matches the informal sense of control or superiority but does not necessarily imply humiliation.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 核心是“算我的”：物品算我的＝拥有；错误算我的＝承担；全场由我掌控＝征服全场。-ed 还可能只是过去分词标记。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Anchor: “It is mine.” A thing is mine: ownership; a mistake is mine: responsibility; the whole stage feels mine: dominance. Remember that -ed can also mark a past participle.

etymology_story.zh: 动词 present 经法语进入英语，源自拉丁语 praesentāre，意为“使在场；呈到面前”，与表示“在场的”的 praesens 有关。把人或事物带到别人面前这一概念，逐渐发展出展示、介绍、赠送、主持及呈现症状等含义。
etymology_story.en: The verb present entered English through French from Latin praesentāre, meaning to make present or bring before someone, related to praesens, meaning “being present.” Bringing someone or something before others developed into showing, introducing, giving, hosting, and displaying symptoms.

morphology_enriched.zh: present（动词）+ -ed → presented，是过去式及过去分词；present 的末音为 /t/，所以 -ed 读 /ɪd/，动词重音仍在第二音节。现代学习中宜把 present 视为完整词基，不机械拆成 pre- + sent。常用词族：presents、presented、presenting；present + -ation → presentation（展示；陈述；颁发）；present + -er → presenter（主持人；报告者）；present + -able → presentable（像样的；适宜见人的）→ presentably（体面地）、presentability（体面程度）；相关词还有 present（名词“礼物”、形容词“在场的；当前的”，均读 /ˈprezənt/）、presence（在场；存在）、presently（不久；目前）和 representation（表述；代表；呈现）。
morphology_enriched.en: Present, the verb, + -ed → presented, its past tense and past participle. Because the base ends in /t/, -ed is pronounced /ɪd/, and the stress remains on the second syllable. Treat present as a whole modern base rather than mechanically splitting it into pre- + sent. Its common family includes presents, presented, presenting, presentation, presenter, presentable, presentably, and presentability. Related words include the noun present, meaning a gift, and the adjective present, meaning here or current, both pronounced /ˈprezənt/; presence; presently; and representation.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: showed（展示了）最宽泛，也可指非正式地给人看；introduced（介绍了）侧重让人初次认识某人或某事；submitted（提交了）强调交给有权审核或决定的人，而 presented 还可强调现场讲解与展示。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Showed is broad and can describe an informal act of letting someone see something. Introduced emphasizes making a person or thing known for the first time. Submitted emphasizes handing something to an authority for review, while presented may also involve explaining or demonstrating it in person.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 核心画面是“带到面前”：把信息带到面前＝展示；把奖品送到面前＝颁发；把人带到面前＝介绍；把困难摆到面前＝构成挑战。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture bringing something before someone: information is shown, an award is given, a person is introduced, and a difficulty becomes a challenge to face.

etymology_story.zh: thousand 源自古英语 þūsend，是继承自日耳曼语族的古老数词，与德语 tausend 等词同源。它一直表示“一千”，复数形式 thousands 后来还广泛用于概指很大的数量。
etymology_story.en: Thousand comes from Old English þūsend, an inherited Germanic numeral related to words such as German tausend. It has retained the meaning 1,000, while its plural thousands is also widely used for an unspecified large quantity.

morphology_enriched.zh: thousand 是现代英语中的单纯数词，不宜拆成有现代意义的词根和词缀。thousand + -s → thousands（数千；若干个千），读 /ˈθaʊzəndz/；thousand + -th → thousandth（第一千；千分之一），读 /ˈθaʊzənθ/；相关构词有 thousandfold（一千倍的；一千倍地）及 thousand-strong（有一千人组成的）。确数后不用 -s，如 three thousand students（三千名学生）；概数用 thousands of students（数千名学生）。
morphology_enriched.en: Thousand is a simple modern numeral and should not be split into supposed meaningful modern components. Thousand + -s → thousands, pronounced /ˈθaʊzəndz/; thousand + -th → thousandth, meaning number 1,000 in a sequence or one part in 1,000, pronounced /ˈθaʊzənθ/. Related formations include thousandfold and thousand-strong. Use the singular form after an exact number, as in three thousand students, but use thousands of students for an unspecified large quantity.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: one thousand（一个千；一千）与 a thousand 数值相同，但 one 可强调精确数量；a grand（非正式：一千元）通常指一千个货币单位，不能泛指一千件任意物品；a multitude（大量）只表示很多，没有“一千”的数值含义。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: One thousand has the same numerical value as a thousand, but one can emphasize an exact count. A grand is informal and normally means a thousand units of money rather than a thousand arbitrary objects. A multitude means a large number without specifying 1,000.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 十个 hundred 就是一个 thousand：确数 two thousand 不加 s；概数 thousands of 表示“一批批的千”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Ten hundreds make one thousand: keep thousand singular in two thousand, but use thousands of for an unspecified number of thousand-sized groups.

etymology_story.zh: rights 的词基 right 源自古英语 riht，其含义包括“直的、正确的、正当的”，相关名词表示正义或应得之物，动词则表示使之端正或纠正。“正当”发展为“权利”，而“恢复正确状态”保留在动词 rights 中。
etymology_story.en: The base right goes back to Old English riht, associated with being straight, correct, or just; related noun and verb uses concerned justice, entitlement, and making something straight or correct. The idea of what is just developed into legal and moral rights, while restoring a proper state remains central to the verb rights.

morphology_enriched.zh: right + -s → rights 有两种常用分析：名词复数“权利等”，或动词第三人称单数“扶正、纠正”；词尾 /t/ 是清辅音，因此 -s 读 /s/。常用词族包括 right、rights、righted、righting；right + -ful → rightful（合法享有的；正当的）→ rightfully、rightfulness；right + -ly → rightly（正确地；理所当然地）；right + -ness → rightness（正确性）；right + -ist → rightist（右翼人士；右翼的）；相关词有 righteous（正直的；正义的）、righteously、righteousness，以及 copyright（版权）、birthright（与生俱来的权利）、rights-holder（权利持有人）、right-wing（右翼的）和 right-handed（惯用右手的）。right 的形容词“正确的；右边的”及副词“向右；恰好”等用法不直接加 -s。
morphology_enriched.en: Right + -s → rights has two common analyses: a plural noun or a third-person singular present-tense verb. Because /t/ is voiceless, -s is pronounced /s/. The common family includes right, rights, righted, righting, rightful, rightfully, rightfulness, rightly, rightness, and rightist. Related forms include righteous, righteously, righteousness, copyright, birthright, rights-holder, right-wing, and right-handed. The adjective and adverb uses of right do not themselves take this -s ending.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: entitlements（应享权益）强调依据法律、规则或身份可获得的具体利益；freedoms（自由）强调不受限制地行动或表达，是 rights 所涵盖的一类；privileges（特权；特殊待遇）强调只授予某些人的优势，未必是人人应享有的权利。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Entitlements emphasize specific benefits due under a law, rule, or status. Freedoms emphasize being able to act or express oneself without restriction and form one category of rights. Privileges are advantages granted to particular people and are not necessarily rights that everyone should enjoy.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 抓住 right 的“正”：正当享有的东西是 rights（权利）；把歪的恢复端正是 rights（扶正）；把不公纠正也是 rights（纠正）。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Anchor everything to right: what is rightfully yours gives rights; making something upright gives rights it; making an injustice right gives rights a wrong.

senses.meaning_en: approval or permission
senses.english_definition: If you give someone the OK, you give them permission to do something.
senses.collocation_en: give the OK; get the OK
senses.collocation_zh: 给予批准；获得许可

senses.meaning_zh: 批准；认可
senses.meaning_en: to approve or authorize
senses.english_definition: If someone OKs a plan or request, they officially agree to it or allow it.
senses.collocation_en: OK a proposal; OK a budget
senses.collocation_zh: 批准一项提议；批准预算
senses.sentence_en: The manager OK'd our request for new equipment.
senses.sentence_zh: 经理批准了我们购置新设备的申请。

etymology_story.zh: OK 于1839年见于美国波士顿的报刊，源于把 all correct 故意拼成 oll korrect 后取首字母的玩笑写法。1840年，美国总统马丁·范布伦的竞选又利用其绰号 Old Kinderhook 的相同首字母，进一步推广了这个词。
etymology_story.en: OK appeared in the Boston press in 1839 as a humorous abbreviation of oll korrect, a deliberate misspelling of all correct. Its spread was reinforced by Martin Van Buren's 1840 presidential campaign, which also used the initials of his nickname Old Kinderhook.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中，OK 是已经词汇化的整词，不能拆成有独立意义的 O 和 K；okay 是其拼写变体。同一形式可转类作形容词、副词、感叹词、名词和动词；名词复数为 OKs，动词形式为 OKs、OK'd／OKed、OKing，okay 对应 okays、okayed、okaying；非正式派生形式有 OK-ish／okayish（还算可以的）。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, OK is a lexicalized whole rather than a combination of meaningful elements O and K; okay is an alternative spelling. Conversion gives adjective, adverb, interjection, noun, and verb uses; forms include plural OKs and verbal OKs, OK'd/OKed, and OKing, with okays, okayed, and okaying for okay; informal derivatives include OK-ish/okayish, meaning fairly acceptable.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: acceptable（可接受的）强调达到最低要求；fine（好的、没问题的）通常比 OK 更积极，但语气会影响含义；approve（批准）对应动词 OK，语体更正式。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Acceptable emphasizes meeting a minimum standard; fine is often more positive than OK, although tone affects its meaning; approve corresponds to the verb OK and is more formal.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把 OK 想成一个“通过”的勾：事情可以、人没事、表示同意、给予批准。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture OK as a check mark: something is acceptable, someone is safe, you agree, or you give approval.

pronunciation.note: 动词 close 的结尾是 /z/，加 -ed 后读 /zd/；不要读成 /st/。

forms: closed 可表示状态；close → closes / closing / closed 是相关动词变化。本课是 be closed 的关闭状态。
family: close v. 关闭；closing n. 关闭过程或结束，亦可作动词 -ing 形式；不等于本课形容词状态。

morphology.text: close（关闭）+ -ed（分词词尾）→ closed：处于关闭状态。close 已有 e，只再加 d。

etymology.text: close 经法语来自拉丁语表示“关上”的词；closed 就像一扇已经关好的门。

usage_note: be closed 表示关闭或不营业。closed 是状态，close 是动词“关闭”；close 作“近的”时读音也不同。

senses.pos: v. 动词（close 的过去式和过去分词）
senses.meaning_zh: 关上；停止营业；结束；完成交易
senses.meaning_en: shut; stopped operating; ended; completed a deal
senses.english_definition: If someone closed something, they shut it, brought it to an end, or completed it; if a business closed, it stopped operating.

etymology_story.zh: closed 由动词 close 加分词词尾形成；close 经古法语 clos、clore 这一词族追溯到拉丁语 claudere，意为“关上”。从实际的门窗关闭，这一意义延伸到停止营业、限制参与以及结束讨论。
etymology_story.en: Closed is formed from the verb close with a participial ending; close came through the Old French family of clos and clore, ultimately from Latin claudere, meaning to shut. Physical shutting extended to stopping business, restricting participation, and ending discussion.

morphology_enriched.zh: close + -ed → closed；close 已有不发音的 e，拼写时只加 d，-ed 在这里读 /d/。closed 既是动词屈折形式，也可作形容词；相关词族包括 closes、closing、closer（关闭者或关闭装置）、closable／closeable（可关闭的）、unclosed（未关闭的）、closedness（封闭性）、closure（关闭；终结）、enclose／enclosure（围住／围合空间）和 disclose／disclosure（披露）；close 作“近的”时读 /kləʊs/，其 closeness 指亲近或接近，应与动词 close /kləʊz/ 区分。
morphology_enriched.en: Close + -ed → closed; because close already ends in silent e, only d is added in spelling, and the ending is pronounced /d/. Closed is both a verbal inflection and an adjective; related family members include closes, closing, closer meaning a person or device that closes, closable/closeable, unclosed, closedness, closure, enclose/enclosure, and disclose/disclosure; adjectival close meaning near is pronounced /kləʊs/ and gives closeness, distinct from verbal close /kləʊz/.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: shut（关着的）与 closed 在门窗等实物上通常可互换；sealed（密封的）强调封严或加封；restricted（受限制的）强调进入或参与受到控制，不一定完全关闭。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Shut is usually interchangeable with closed for physical objects such as doors; sealed emphasizes secure fastening or a barrier against passage; restricted emphasizes controlled access or participation without necessarily implying complete closure.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: close 是“关”，closed 是“已经关上”：门关了、店停业了、参与受限了、事情结束了。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Close means shut; closed presents the result: a door is shut, a shop is unavailable, access is limited, or a matter is finished.

pos: adj. 形容词（bad 的比较级）

pronunciation.label: 英式教学读法
pronunciation.note: 按所列英式音标朗读；重音符号标出重读音节。

forms: bad → worse → worst：差、更差、最差。不用 more worse，比较对象常接 than。
family: worst adj. 最差的；worsen v. 恶化、使变糟；worsening 可为动词 -ing 形式。

morphology.text: bad（差） + 不规则比较级变化 → worse（更差）；bad → worse → worst 是不规则比较变化，worse 整词记忆，不是给 bad 加普通后缀。

etymology.text: worse 来自古英语表示“更差”的词形；把 bad、worse、worst 当作一条逐步变差的线来记。

usage_note: 本课比较两种情况的好坏，常见 worse than、get worse。不用 badder 或 more worse。

senses.sentence_zh: 我们本以为危机已经结束，但后面还有更糟的事。

etymology_story.zh: worse 源自古英语 wyrsa 等表示“更坏”的比较级形式，属于古老的日耳曼语词族。它与 bad 并非由同一个现代词根按规则构成，而是在现代英语中充当 bad、badly 的不规则比较级，并与最高级 worst 配套使用。
etymology_story.en: Worse descends from Old English comparative forms such as wyrsa, meaning more bad, and belongs to an old Germanic word family. It is not formed regularly from the modern root bad, but serves as the irregular comparative of bad and badly, alongside the superlative worst.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代形式按整体记忆，不把 worse 拆成 bad + 后缀：形容词 bad → worse → worst，副词 badly → worse → worst；ill 表示身体不适时，比较级也常用 worse。相关词族包括 badness（恶劣；坏的程度）、worse + -en → worsen（恶化；使恶化）、worsens、worsened、worsening，以及复合词 worst-case（最坏情况的）；worsen 构词时去掉 worse 末尾的 e。
morphology_enriched.en: Learn worse as a whole rather than as bad plus a suffix: the adjective series is bad → worse → worst, and the adverb series is badly → worse → worst; ill also commonly takes worse when referring to health. Related forms include badness, worse + -en → worsen, with final e dropped, worsens, worsened, worsening, and the compound worst-case.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: poorer（更差的）常比较质量、表现或条件；inferior（较差的）较正式，表示低于某个标准，通常接 to；more serious（更严重的）强调问题或病情的严重程度，而 worse 的适用范围更广。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Poorer often compares quality, performance, or conditions; inferior is more formal, indicates a lower standard, and typically takes to; more serious focuses on the severity of a problem or illness, whereas worse has a broader range.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 沿着变差的阶梯记：bad 差 → worse 更差 → worst 最差；动作做得差则从 badly 起步。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Follow a downward staircase: bad → worse → worst; for how an action is done, start with badly.

senses.meaning_zh: 三十
senses.meaning_en: the number 30
senses.english_definition: Thirty is the number that comes after twenty-nine and before thirty-one.
senses.collocation_en: thirty minutes; thirty people
senses.collocation_zh: 三十分钟；三十个人
senses.sentence_en: The journey takes about thirty minutes.
senses.sentence_zh: 这段路程大约需要三十分钟。

senses.pos: n. 名词（通常用复数 thirties）
senses.meaning_zh: 三十多岁；某世纪的三十年代；三十至三十九的数值范围
senses.meaning_en: ages, years, or values from thirty through thirty-nine
senses.english_definition: Someone's thirties are the years when they are aged thirty to thirty-nine; the thirties can also refer to the corresponding decade of a century or a range of numerical values.
senses.collocation_en: in her thirties; in the nineteen-thirties
senses.collocation_zh: 在她三十多岁时；在二十世纪三十年代
senses.sentence_en: She started her own business in her early thirties.
senses.sentence_zh: 她三十出头时创办了自己的企业。

etymology_story.zh: thirty 来自古英语 þrītig，其中前一部分表示“三”，后一部分表示“十的组数”。它原本的构词逻辑就是“三组十”，经过语音和拼写演变成为今天的 thirty。
etymology_story.en: Thirty comes from Old English þrītig, combining an element meaning three with an element referring to groups of ten. Its original structure meant three tens and developed into the modern form through changes in pronunciation and spelling.

morphology_enriched.zh: 可按 thir-（与 three“三”同源的变体）+ -ty（数词中表示“十的倍数”的成分）理解，但它不是把现代 three 直接加后缀得到的规则拼写。常见相关形式有 thirty + -th → thirtieth（第三十，y 改 ie）、thirty + -s → thirties（复数，y 改 ies）、thirtyish（三十左右的）、thirtyfold（三十倍的），以及 thirty-one 至 thirty-nine、thirty-first、thirty-year-old 等复合形式；three、third、thirteen 属于相关数词词族。
morphology_enriched.en: The structure can be understood as thir-, a historical variant related to three, plus -ty, the numeral element for multiples of ten, rather than a regular spelling formed directly from modern three. Common related forms include thirtieth, with y changed to ie before -th, thirties, with y changed to ies for the plural, thirtyish, thirtyfold, and compounds such as thirty-one through thirty-nine, thirty-first, and thirty-year-old; three, third, and thirteen belong to the related numeral family.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: thirty 是普通词语写法；30 是完全相同数值的阿拉伯数字写法；three tens（三个十）是解释数量构成的表达，通常不直接替代日常句子里的 thirty。这类精确数词没有通常意义上的两三个近义词。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Thirty is the ordinary word form; 30 is the Arabic-numeral representation of exactly the same value; three tens explains its composition and is not usually a direct replacement in everyday sentences. An exact numeral does not have two or three ordinary lexical synonyms.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: thir- 联想到 three，-ty 联想到“几十”：三个十就是三十；重音在前，区别于通常重音在后的 thirteen。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Connect thir- with three and -ty with tens: three tens make thirty; its first-syllable stress helps distinguish it from thirteen, which usually has final stress.

etymology_story.zh: 表示“妈妈”的 mum 属于 mam、mamma 等亲昵称呼的词族，与婴幼儿容易发出的声音有关；表示“缄默”的 mum 则源于另一类模仿闭口含混声的表达。美式英语中表示“菊花”的 mum 是 chrysanthemum 的截短形式，这三个意思并非由同一个词义逐步演变而来。
etymology_story.en: Mum meaning mother belongs to the family of affectionate nursery forms such as mam and mamma, associated with sounds young children readily make; mum meaning silent has a separate expressive origin connected with a closed-mouth sound. American mum meaning chrysanthemum is a shortening of chrysanthemum, so the three meanings do not represent a single chain of semantic development.

morphology_enriched.zh: mum 表示“妈妈”时是现代不可再拆分的词干，复数 mums，所有格 mum's；常见亲昵形式为 mummy，复数 mummies，形容词 mumsy 表示“显得像传统母亲的”，有时含不够时髦之意；美式 mom、mommy 是对应称呼，并非由 mum 加后缀形成。表示“缄默”的 mum 是独立词项，常见于 keep mum 和 mum's the word（务必保密），其中 mum's 是 mum is 的缩写；花名 mum 则由 chrysanthemum 截短而成，复数也是 mums。
morphology_enriched.en: Mum meaning mother is a simple modern stem, with plural mums and possessive mum's; related affectionate forms include mummy and plural mummies, while mumsy means conventionally motherly and can suggest an unfashionable appearance; American mom and mommy are corresponding forms rather than suffixal derivatives of mum. Silent mum is a separate item found in keep mum and mum's the word, where mum's contracts mum is; the flower name mum is clipped from chrysanthemum and also has the plural mums.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: mother（母亲）较中性或正式，mum（妈妈）亲切且主要用于英式英语，mom 是主要美式对应形式；在“缄默”义中，silent 泛指不说话，tight-lipped 强调不愿透露信息。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Mother is more neutral or formal, mum is affectionate and chiefly British, and mom is the main American equivalent; for the silent sense, silent broadly means not speaking, while tight-lipped emphasizes unwillingness to reveal information.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 三个独立画面：英国孩子喊 Mum；双唇闭紧就 keep mum；美国秋日门廊摆着 mums 菊花。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Use three separate pictures: a British child calls Mum; closed lips keep mum; American autumn porches display mums.

etymology_story.zh: Sunday 来自古英语 sunnandæg，字面意思是“太阳之日”，是对拉丁语“太阳之日”这一星期名称的仿译。这个名称保留了古代以天体命名星期的传统。
etymology_story.en: Sunday comes from Old English sunnandæg, literally 'the sun's day,' a translation of the Latin weekday name meaning 'day of the sun.' It preserves the ancient practice of naming weekdays after heavenly bodies.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代可识别为词汇化合成词 sun（太阳）+ day（日），但 Sunday 是固定的星期名称。复数 Sundays /ˈsʌndeɪz/ 表示多个星期日，也可作副词表示“每逢星期日”；常见合成表达有 Sunday school（主日学校）和 Sunday best（最好的衣服，原指星期日礼拜时穿的盛装）。Sunday service 等表达中的 Sunday 通常按名词作定语分析；没有常用的派生动词。
morphology_enriched.en: The modern word is a lexicalized compound, sun + day, functioning as a fixed weekday name. The plural Sundays /ˈsʌndeɪz/ means multiple Sundays and can also function adverbially to mean 'every Sunday'; common compounds include Sunday school and Sunday best, originally one's finest clothes worn for Sunday worship. Sunday in expressions such as Sunday service is generally analyzed as an attributive noun; there is no common derived verb.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: Sunday 没有完全等义的普通近义词。the Lord's Day（主日）是基督教语境中对星期日的称呼；the Sabbath（安息日）强调宗教休息与敬拜，其对应日期因传统而异，不能一概替换 Sunday。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Sunday has no exact everyday synonym. The Lord's Day is a Christian name for Sunday; the Sabbath emphasizes religious rest and worship, and its calendar day varies by tradition, so it is not universally interchangeable with Sunday.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: sun（太阳）+ day（日）：太阳之日，就是星期日。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Sun + day: picture the sun shining over Sunday.

etymology_story.zh: prince 经古法语来自拉丁语 princeps，意为“首位的人、首领”，其构词与“第一”和“取得、占据”的词根有关。它后来发展为统治者、贵族及王室男性成员的称号，也引申指某一群体中的杰出人物。
etymology_story.en: Prince came through Old French from Latin princeps, meaning 'first person' or 'leader,' historically formed from elements connected with 'first' and 'take.' It developed into a title for rulers, nobles, and male royalty, and figuratively for outstanding people.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 prince 是不可再按常用词缀拆分的词基；prince + -s → princes /ˈprɪnsɪz/（复数）。常见词族有 princess（公主；王妃）、princely（王子般的；豪华的；数额巨大的）和 princedom（王公身份或领地）；principality（公国）属于历史相关词，不是现代英语中直接由 prince 加后缀构成的词。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, prince is a base without a productive internal affix breakdown; prince + -s gives princes /ˈprɪnsɪz/. Common family members include princess, princely, and princedom; principality is historically related rather than a straightforward modern suffixation of prince.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: royal（王室成员）范围更广，不限男性；monarch（君主）强调实际的国家元首身份，王子通常不是 monarch；sovereign（拥有主权的君主）强调独立统治权，只适用于 prince 的部分君主义项。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: A royal is any member of a royal family, regardless of gender; a monarch is the reigning head of a monarchy, which most princes are not; a sovereign emphasizes independent ruling authority and overlaps only with the ruling sense of prince.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 从“居首的首领”联想到“王公、王子”，再联想到“人中俊杰”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Start with 'the foremost person': a leader, then a royal prince, then someone outstanding.

etymology_story.zh: born 来自古英语 boren，是 beran（承载、携带；生育）的过去分词。现代英语逐渐区分 born 和 borne：被动表达出生通常用 born，而携带、承受以及主动完成时表达生育通常用 borne。
etymology_story.en: Born descends from Old English boren, the past participle of beran, meaning 'carry' or 'give birth.' Modern English developed a distinction between born, normally used for birth in passive constructions, and borne, used for carrying, enduring, and giving birth in active perfect constructions.

morphology_enriched.zh: born 是 bear 的不规则过去分词：bear—bore—born/borne，不是 bore + -n 的能产构词。常见相关形式有 unborn（尚未出生的）、newborn（新生的；新生儿）、reborn（重生的）、inborn（天生的）、stillborn（死产的；未能实现的）、firstborn（头生的；长子或长女）和 -born 合成词，如 French-born（出生于法国的）；bear 的其他常见词族有 bearing（承载；举止；方位）、bearer（携带者）和 childbearing（生育）。
morphology_enriched.en: Born is an irregular past participle of bear: bear—bore—born/borne, rather than a productive formation of bore + -n. Common related forms include unborn, newborn, reborn, inborn, stillborn, firstborn, and compounds in -born such as French-born; other common members of the bear family include bearing, bearer, and childbearing.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: delivered（被接生的）强调分娩或接生过程；innate（先天的）修饰与生俱来的特征，而 born 常用于 a born leader 一类人物评价；arise（产生）可对应比喻义，但它是主动动词，不使用 be born 的结构。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Delivered emphasizes the process of childbirth; innate describes an inborn quality, whereas born often evaluates a person, as in a born leader; arise overlaps with the figurative meaning 'begin to exist' but uses an active verb construction.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: bear 有“生育”义：be born 是被带到世上；天赋随出生而来，就是 a born leader。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Bear can mean 'give birth': be born means being brought into the world; a born leader seems to arrive with the talent.

etymology_story.zh: Christmas 来自古英语 Cristes mæsse，意思是“基督的弥撒”。这个名称起初指纪念基督诞生的宗教礼仪，后来也指整个节日及其周围的庆祝期间。
etymology_story.en: Christmas comes from Old English Cristes mæsse, meaning 'Christ's mass.' The name originally referred to the religious service commemorating Christ's birth and later also came to denote the festival and its surrounding holiday period.

morphology_enriched.zh: Christmas 是已词汇化的历史合成词，与 Christ（基督）和 Mass（弥撒）有关；中间的 s 历史上来自所有格，不能当作现代复数后缀。Christmas + -es → Christmases /ˈkrɪsməsɪz/，表示多个圣诞节；相关形式有 Christmassy、Christmasy（有圣诞气氛的）、Christmastime（圣诞时节）、Christmas Eve（平安夜）和 Christmas Day（圣诞节当天），Xmas 是缩写形式；Christmas tree 中的 Christmas 是名词作定语。
morphology_enriched.en: Christmas is a lexicalized historical compound connected with Christ and Mass; its internal s historically marks possession, not a modern plural. Christmas + -es gives Christmases /ˈkrɪsməsɪz/; related forms include Christmassy, Christmasy, Christmastime, Christmas Eve, and Christmas Day, while Xmas is an abbreviation. Christmas functions attributively as a noun in Christmas tree.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: Xmas 是 Christmas 的缩写，常见于非正式文字；Christmastime 强调圣诞节前后的时段；Yuletide 是偏文学或传统风格的“圣诞时节”，不如 Christmas 日常。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Xmas is an abbreviation commonly used in informal writing; Christmastime emphasizes the period around Christmas; Yuletide is a literary or traditional term for the Christmas season.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: Christ（基督）+ Mass（弥撒）：由纪念基督的礼仪联想到圣诞节。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Christ + Mass: a service honoring Christ gives its name to Christmas.

etymology_story.zh: liked 是 like 的规则过去式和过去分词；动词 like 来自古英语 līcian，原义为“使人愉快、合某人的意”。早期常以令人愉快的事物作主语，后来逐渐发展为现代以感受者作主语的用法，网络时代又产生了“点赞”义。
etymology_story.en: Liked is the regular past tense and past participle of like, whose verb descends from Old English līcian, meaning 'please' or 'be pleasing to.' Earlier constructions often made the pleasing thing the subject, before the modern experiencer-subject pattern developed; the social media sense arose much later.

morphology_enriched.zh: like + -ed → liked：词尾已有不发音的 e，因此拼写只加 d；词干以清辅音 /k/ 结尾，过去式后缀读 /t/，全词读 /laɪkt/，不增加音节。liked 是屈折形式，不是独立的派生词；常见词族有 likes、liking、likable/likeable（讨人喜欢的）、likability/likeability（讨喜程度）、dislike、disliked、disliking、unlikable/unlikeable（不讨人喜欢的）及复合形容词 well-liked（受欢迎的）；名词 a like 表示一个赞。
morphology_enriched.en: Like + -ed gives liked: because like already ends in silent e, only d is added in spelling. After voiceless /k/, the ending is pronounced /t/, giving the single syllable /laɪkt/. Liked is an inflected form rather than a separate derivative; common family members include likes, liking, likable/likeable, likability/likeability, dislike, disliked, disliking, unlikable/unlikeable, and the compound adjective well-liked; the noun a like denotes an online expression of approval.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: enjoyed（喜欢、享受）更强调活动或体验带来的愉悦；was fond of（喜爱）强调对人或事物较温和而持久的感情；approved of（赞同）强调认可或认为合适，并不一定表示享受或喜爱。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Enjoyed emphasizes pleasure from an activity or experience; was fond of suggests warm, often lasting affection; approved of expresses acceptance or a favorable judgment without necessarily implying pleasure or affection.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: like 的 e 留着，只加 d；/k/ 后接 /t/：liked，把喜欢放进过去。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Keep like's e, add d, and say /t/ after /k/: liked places liking in the past.

etymology_story.zh: missed 是 miss 的规则过去式和过去分词；miss 源自古英语 missan，表示“未击中、未得到或未能做到”。“没有接触到或得到”的核心意义逐渐延伸出错过、漏察以及因某人不在而想念等用法。
etymology_story.en: Missed is the regular past tense and past participle of miss, which comes from Old English missan, meaning to fail to hit, obtain, or achieve something. The central idea of failing to connect developed into missing events, overlooking details, and feeling someone's absence.

morphology_enriched.zh: missed = miss + -ed；这是屈折变化，不是新的派生词。miss 以清辅音 /s/ 结尾，因此 -ed 读 /t/，全词读 /mɪst/。主要词形和词族：miss、misses、missed、missing；形容词 missing（缺失的）、missable（可能错过的；不值得特别看的）、unmissable（不容错过的）；相关表达 miss out（错过）、near miss（险些发生的事故）。称谓 Miss（小姐）来源不同。
morphology_enriched.en: Missed = miss + -ed; this is inflection rather than the formation of a new derived word. Because miss ends in voiceless /s/, -ed is pronounced /t/, giving /mɪst/. Principal forms and family members include miss, misses, missed, missing, the adjective missing, missable, and unmissable; related expressions include miss out and near miss. The title Miss has a different origin.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: overlooked（忽略了）强调未注意到细节；failed to catch（没赶上／没接住）强调未能及时赶上或接到；longed for（渴望、思念）与表示想念的 missed 接近，但情感通常更强烈。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Overlooked emphasizes failing to notice a detail; failed to catch emphasizes not reaching or receiving something in time; longed for overlaps with missed in the sense of feeling someone's absence, but usually expresses stronger desire.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 抓住“没接上”：没接上车是错过，没接上目标是未击中，没接上相聚便会想念；-ed 把动作放到过去。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Think of a connection that did not happen: with a bus, you missed it; with a target, you missed it; with a loved one, you missed them. The ending -ed places the action in the past.

etymology_story.zh: Saturday 源自古英语 Sæternesdæg，字面意思是“萨图恩之日”，对应拉丁语的“萨图恩之日”。萨图恩是古罗马神祇，其名字也用于土星；这一星期名称保留了古罗马以天体及相关神祇命名日期的传统。
etymology_story.en: Saturday comes from Old English Sæternesdæg, literally 'Saturn's day,' corresponding to the Latin name for that day. Saturn was a Roman god whose name was also given to the planet, and the weekday preserves the Roman tradition of naming days after celestial bodies and their associated deities.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 Saturday 通常作为完整词学习；历史构词可理解为 Saturn 的名称形式 + day，而不是现代可自由拆分的前缀和词根。主要形式：Saturday；复数 Saturdays（多个星期六，也常在时间表达中表示每逢星期六）；缩写 Sat.。相关组合有 Saturday night（星期六晚上）和 Saturday-night（用于名词前的复合修饰语）。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, Saturday is normally learned as a whole word; historically, it combines a form of Saturn's name with day rather than a productive modern prefix and root. Principal forms are Saturday, plural Saturdays, which can also express a recurring Saturday schedule, and the abbreviation Sat. Related combinations include Saturday night and the compound modifier Saturday-night.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: Saturday 没有另一个完全同义的常用单词。Sat. 是书面缩写；the sixth day of the week（按星期一为首日计算的一周第六天）是解释性说法；a weekend day（周末的一天）范围更宽，也可能指星期日。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Saturday has no separate everyday word that is an exact synonym. Sat. is its written abbreviation; the sixth day of the week is an explanatory phrase when Monday is counted first; a weekend day is broader and may also refer to Sunday.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: Saturn（土星／萨图恩）之 day（日）→ Saturday；把星期六想成日历上的“土星日”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Saturn's day became Saturday: picture a small Saturn on the Saturday square of a calendar.

etymology_story.zh: queen 来自古英语 cwēn，曾表示“女人、妻子、王后或女王”，属于古老的日耳曼语词汇。其意义逐渐集中于地位最高的女性，后来又用于昆虫群体的繁殖雌虫、棋子和某领域的杰出女性。
etymology_story.en: Queen comes from Old English cwēn, which could mean a woman, wife, queen consort, or female ruler, and belongs to an ancient Germanic word family. Its meaning became centered on a woman of supreme rank and later extended to reproductive insects, game pieces, and outstanding women in particular fields.

morphology_enriched.zh: queen 在现代英语中是不可再拆分的自由词根；名词和动词之间有零派生关系。主要词形与派生词：queens、queened、queening；queen + -ly → queenly（女王般的）；queenly + -ness → queenliness（女王般的仪态）；queen + -ship → queenship（女王或王后的身份）；queen + -dom → queendom（女王统治的王国或领域）。常见复合词有 queen bee、queen-size、queen-sized。
morphology_enriched.en: Queen is a free root with no productive internal breakdown in modern English; its noun and verb uses are related by conversion. Principal forms and derivatives include queens, queened, queening, queen + -ly → queenly, queenly + -ness → queenliness, queen + -ship → queenship, and queen + -dom → queendom. Common compounds include queen bee, queen-size, and queen-sized.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: monarch（君主）不限定性别；sovereign（君主、最高统治者）更正式，强调最高统治地位；consort（君主的配偶）强调婚姻身份，因此 queen consort 是王后，不等于独立执政的女王。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Monarch is gender-neutral; sovereign is more formal and emphasizes supreme ruling status; consort identifies a monarch's spouse, so a queen consort is distinguished from a queen who reigns in her own right.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 核心画面是“居于核心或最高位置的女性”：国家有女王，蜂群有蜂王，棋盘上有行动强大的后。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture a female figure at the center or top: a queen in a kingdom, a queen in a hive, and a powerful queen on a chessboard.

etymology_story.zh: twelve 来自古英语 twelf，其日耳曼语祖形通常被解释为“余下两个”，即数完十个后还剩两个。现代英语中的 twelve 已是完整的数词，不能按现代词缀任意拆解。
etymology_story.en: Twelve comes from Old English twelf, whose Germanic ancestor is generally interpreted as 'two left over,' meaning two remaining after counting ten. In modern English, twelve is a complete number word rather than a combination of productive modern affixes.

morphology_enriched.zh: twelve 是现代英语中的单纯数词；作数词时不因后面的名词为复数而加 -s，如 twelve books。名词复数为 twelves；序数词为 twelfth（第十二），其名词复数为 twelfths（十二分之一的若干份）。相关构词有 twelvefold（十二倍的／地）、twelvemonth（一年，较旧或文学用法）、twelve-year-old（十二岁的）。dozen（一打）意义相关，但不是 twelve 的派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: Twelve is a simple number word in modern English; as a numeral it takes no plural -s before a plural noun, as in twelve books. Its noun plural is twelves; the ordinal is twelfth, with the noun plural twelfths for multiple twelfth parts. Related formations include twelvefold, twelvemonth, an older or literary word for a year, and twelve-year-old. Dozen is related in meaning but is not derived from twelve.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: a dozen（一打）在计数时等于十二，但通常作为数量名词短语使用；12 是同一数值的数字写法；a group of twelve（十二个组成的一组）强调一个群组，而不是数值本身。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: A dozen equals twelve in counting but normally functions as a quantity noun phrase; 12 is the numeral representing the same value; a group of twelve emphasizes a collection rather than the abstract number.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 十个数完，再余两个：10 + 2 = twelve；一年十二个月也能固定这个数量。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Count ten, then two left over: 10 + 2 = twelve. The twelve months of a year reinforce the number.

etymology_story.zh: 亲属称谓 grandfather 形成于中古英语时期，由 grand 与 father 组合，受法语同类亲属称谓影响。表示“保留旧规”的动词用法源于 grandfather clause：美国历史上有此类条款以祖辈的投票资格等条件豁免新限制，并被用于剥夺黑人选民的权利；后来该表达泛化为对既有对象的豁免。
etymology_story.en: The family term grandfather developed in Middle English from grand and father, influenced by comparable French kinship terms. The verb meaning to preserve an exemption comes from grandfather clause, historically used in the United States to exempt people from voting restrictions through ancestral qualifications while disenfranchising Black voters; the expression later broadened to exemptions for existing cases.

morphology_enriched.zh: grandfather = grand-（亲属关系中比父母再高一代）+ father（父亲）。主要词形和派生形式：grandfathers、grandfathered、grandfathering、grandfatherly（祖父般的）。相关亲属构词包括 grandmother（祖母／外祖母）、grandparent（祖父母或外祖父母之一）、grandparents（祖父母／外祖父母）、great-grandfather（曾祖父／曾外祖父）。固定组合 grandfather clock 指落地式长摆钟，其中 grandfather 作名词修饰语。
morphology_enriched.en: Grandfather = grand-, marking a generation above a parent in this kinship term, + father. Principal forms and derivatives include grandfathers, grandfathered, grandfathering, and grandfatherly. Related kinship formations include grandmother, grandparent, grandparents, and great-grandfather. In the established compound grandfather clock, meaning a tall freestanding pendulum clock, grandfather functions as a noun modifier.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: grandpa 和 grandad 都是 grandfather 的亲昵称呼，grandad 尤常见于英式英语；forebear（祖先）范围更广，可以指更早世代的男性或女性。动词义可用 exempt（豁免）近似表达，但 grandfather 特别强调因原有身份或安排而继续适用旧条件。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Grandpa and grandad are affectionate informal equivalents of grandfather, with grandad especially associated with British English; forebear is broader and can refer to male or female ancestors from earlier generations. For the verb, exempt is a near equivalent, but grandfather specifically emphasizes retaining earlier conditions because a person or arrangement already existed.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 亲属义：在 father 上再往上一代，就是 grandfather；动词义：把“老资格”连接到“沿用老规则”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: For the family meaning, move one generation above father. For the verb, connect an established status with keeping the established rules.

etymology_story.zh: willing 源于中古英语中动词 will 的分词形式；该动词承自古英语 willan，意为“想要、希望”。分词后来固定为形容词，表示出于本人意愿、愿意行动或配合。
etymology_story.en: Willing developed from a participial form of Middle English will, a verb inherited from Old English willan, meaning 'to wish or desire.' The participle became an established adjective describing someone who acts by choice or is ready to cooperate.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：will（想要；以意志促使；立遗嘱赠予）+ -ing → willing，可作现在分词，也已词汇化为形容词。常用派生：willingly（乐意地）、willingness（意愿）、unwilling（不愿意的）、unwillingly（不情愿地）、unwillingness（不情愿）；相关同族词有 will（意愿；遗嘱）、willpower（意志力）、willful/wilful（故意的；任性的）和 willfulness/wilfulness（故意；任性）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: will ('desire,' 'make happen through determination,' or 'leave by testament') + -ing → willing, both a present participle and an established adjective. Common derivatives are willingly, willingness, unwilling, unwillingly, and unwillingness; related family members include will, willpower, willful/wilful, and willfulness/wilfulness.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 形容词义：ready（准备好且愿意）强调已具备行动条件；eager（热切的）比 willing 表达更强的期待与热情；amenable（愿意配合的）侧重接受建议或安排。willing 本身只说明有意愿，不一定热情高涨。遗赠动词义可用 bequeath（以遗嘱赠予）。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: For the adjective, ready emphasizes preparedness as well as willingness; eager expresses stronger enthusiasm; amenable emphasizes openness to suggestions or arrangements. Willing itself indicates consent or readiness without necessarily implying excitement. In the inheritance sense, bequeath means to leave something by will.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: will 是“意愿”：willing 就是“心里愿意，行动肯配合”；作动词分词时，可联想到“用意志推动”或“用遗嘱安排”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Connect willing with will: your own will makes you ready to act; as a verb form, it can describe directing mental effort or arranging a gift through a will.

etymology_story.zh: Monday 来自古英语 mōnandæg，字面意思是“月亮之日”，由表示“月亮”的词的所有格与 dæg（一天）组成。这一名称仿照拉丁语“月亮之日”的命名方式，后来演变成现代拼写 Monday。
etymology_story.en: Monday comes from Old English mōnandæg, literally 'the moon's day,' combining the genitive form of the word for 'moon' with dæg, 'day.' It followed the Latin naming pattern 'day of the moon' and later developed its modern spelling.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 Monday 是固定的星期名称，没有能产性的前缀或后缀；历史上对应 moon（月亮）+ day（日），但不能按现代读音直接拼合。常用形式：Mondays（多个星期一；每逢星期一）、Monday's（星期一的）、Mondays'（多个星期一的）；没有常用的标准派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, Monday is a fixed weekday name without a productive prefix or suffix; historically it corresponds to moon + day, although its modern pronunciation is not a straightforward combination of those words. Common forms are Mondays ('more than one Monday' or 'every Monday'), Monday's, and Mondays'; it has no common standard derivatives.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 没有意义完全相同的普通近义词。Mon. 是 Monday 的书面缩写；on Monday 表示“在星期一”；on Mondays 通常表示“每逢星期一”，强调重复发生，不能在所有语境中与单数形式互换。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: There are no ordinary exact synonyms. Mon. is a written abbreviation of Monday; on Monday identifies the weekday of an event; on Mondays usually describes a recurring weekly event and is not interchangeable with the singular in every context.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: Monday＝历史上的“月亮之日”：想象星期一的日历格上画着一轮月亮。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Monday is historically the moon's day: picture a moon drawn in the Monday square of a calendar.

etymology_story.zh: Friday 来自古英语 Frīgedæg，意为“女神 Frīg 之日”，其中 dæg 意为“一天”。这一名称以日耳曼女神 Frīg 对应罗马女神维纳斯，仿照拉丁语“维纳斯之日”的星期命名方式。
etymology_story.en: Friday comes from Old English Frīgedæg, meaning 'Frīg's day,' with dæg meaning 'day.' The name followed the Latin pattern 'day of Venus,' substituting the Germanic goddess Frīg for the Roman goddess.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 Friday 是固定的星期名称；历史结构为 Frīg（女神名）的所有格形式 + day（日），Fri- 不是表示“自由”或“油炸”的词根。常用形式：Fridays（多个星期五；每逢星期五）、Friday's（星期五的）、Fridays'（多个星期五的）；没有常用的标准派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, Friday is a fixed weekday name; historically it combines a possessive form of the goddess's name Frīg with day. Fri- is not a root meaning 'free' or 'fry.' Common forms are Fridays ('more than one Friday' or 'every Friday'), Friday's, and Fridays'; it has no common standard derivatives.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 没有意义完全相同的普通近义词。Fri. 是 Friday 的书面缩写；on Friday 表示“在星期五”；on Fridays 通常表示“每逢星期五”。Good Friday 指复活节前的“耶稣受难日”，不能泛指任何一个星期五。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: There are no ordinary exact synonyms. Fri. is a written abbreviation of Friday; on Friday identifies the weekday of an event; on Fridays usually expresses weekly repetition. Good Friday names the Christian observance before Easter and does not mean any Friday.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: Friday＝Frīg 女神之日：用“女神名 + day”记住历史来源。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Friday is Frīg's day: remember the historical pattern 'goddess's name + day.'

senses.meaning_zh: 惊吓；突如其来的恐惧
senses.meaning_en: sudden fear or an experience that causes it
senses.english_definition: Fright is a sudden feeling of fear, and a fright is something that makes you feel suddenly afraid.
senses.collocation_en: give someone a fright; get a fright
senses.collocation_zh: 吓某人一跳；受到惊吓
senses.sentence_en: You gave me a fright when you opened the door so suddenly.

senses.pos: n. 名词（非正式用法，尤用于英式英语）
senses.meaning_zh: 样子难看或邋遢的人；难看的东西
senses.meaning_en: a person or thing that looks very unattractive or untidy
senses.english_definition: If you say that someone looks a fright, you mean that they look very unattractive or untidy.
senses.collocation_en: look a fright; look an absolute fright
senses.collocation_zh: 样子很难看或很邋遢；样子糟糕透了
senses.sentence_en: After a night without sleep, I looked an absolute fright.
senses.sentence_zh: 一夜没睡之后，我看上去糟糕透了。

etymology_story.zh: fright 承自古英语 fyrhtu，意为“恐惧、惊惧”，后来经过语音和拼写变化形成今天的词形。它保留了“恐惧”的核心意义，也可指一次惊吓，并引申为外表令人吃惊的难看人物或事物。
etymology_story.en: Fright descends from Old English fyrhtu, meaning 'fear or dread,' with later changes in pronunciation and spelling producing the modern form. It retained its core meaning of fear, came to denote an individual scare, and also developed an informal sense referring to an unattractive person or thing.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：fright 是基础词；fright + -en → frighten（使害怕）；frighten + -ed → frightened（害怕的）；frighten + -ing → frightening（令人害怕的）；frightening + -ly → frighteningly（令人害怕地）。另有 fright + -ful → frightful（可怕的；糟糕的）、frightfully（可怕地；非常）和 frightfulness（可怕；糟糕）；名词复数为 frights（多次惊吓）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: fright is a base word; fright + -en → frighten; frighten + -ed → frightened; frighten + -ing → frightening; frightening + -ly → frighteningly. Other derivatives are fright + -ful → frightful ('terrifying' or 'very unpleasant'), frightfully ('terrifyingly' or 'very'), and frightfulness; the plural noun is frights.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: fear（恐惧）是范围最广的词，可以持续很久；scare（惊吓）常指一次使人害怕的事件或体验，语气较口语化；terror（极度恐惧）强调强烈程度。fright 尤其常表示突然受到的惊吓。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Fear is the broadest term and may be long-lasting; scare often denotes a particular frightening event or experience and is more conversational; terror emphasizes extreme intensity. Fright is especially associated with sudden fear.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: fright 是“吓一跳”；加 -en 成 frighten，就是“使人吓一跳”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Fright is the sudden fear you feel; add -en to make frighten, meaning to cause that fear.

pronunciation.label: 美式教学读法
pronunciation.note: 重读第二音节；末尾是轻读的 /ən/。

forms: 表示数量时用 eleven，后接复数名词；序数词 eleventh 表示第十一。elevens 是名词用法的复数，不用于 eleven books 这样的数量短语。
family: eleventh 序数词：第十一；elevenths 可作名词，表示多个十一分之一。

morphology.text: eleven（十一）+ -th（序数后缀）→ eleventh：第十一。数量与次序要分开。

etymology.text: eleven 来自古英语的数词，经过中古英语演变成今天的拼写。助记：十个手指之外再加一个，就是 eleven。

usage_note: eleven 回答 how many；eleventh 回答排第几。eleven students 后的 students 要用复数。

senses.meaning_zh: 十一人球队，尤指板球队或足球队
senses.meaning_en: a team of eleven players, especially in cricket or football
senses.english_definition: An eleven is a team of eleven players, especially a cricket or football team.
senses.collocation_en: the first eleven; the school eleven
senses.collocation_zh: 第一队；学校的十一人球队

etymology_story.zh: eleven 来自古英语 endleofan，其日耳曼语祖形通常解释为“剩下一个”，即数完十个后还多出一个。它经过中古英语时期的语音和拼写变化，形成了现代词形。
etymology_story.en: Eleven comes from Old English endleofan, whose Germanic ancestor is traditionally interpreted as 'one left over,' meaning one remaining after ten has been counted. Changes in pronunciation and spelling through Middle English produced the modern form.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 eleven 是不可按现成词根和词缀继续拆分的基本数词。eleven + -th → eleventh（第十一；十一分之一）；eleventh + -s → elevenths（若干个十一分之一）；eleven + -s → elevens（多个数字十一；多支十一人球队）；相关复合词 elevenfold 表示“十一倍的；十一倍地”。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, eleven is a basic numeral that cannot be productively divided into current roots and affixes. Eleven + -th → eleventh ('11th' or 'one of eleven equal parts'); eleventh + -s → elevenths; eleven + -s → elevens ('instances of the number 11' or 'teams of eleven players'); the related compound elevenfold means 'eleven times as great' or 'by a factor of eleven.'

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 数值义没有普通近义词：11 是数字写法，XI 是罗马数字写法，均表示同一数值。球队义中，team（球队）不限定人数；side（参赛一方或球队）强调比赛中的一方；eleven 明确指由十一名上场球员组成的队伍。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: The numerical sense has no ordinary synonyms: 11 is the digit form and XI is the Roman numeral form of the same value. In the sporting sense, team does not specify the number of players; side emphasizes one competing group; eleven specifically identifies a team of eleven players.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 十个数完，还剩一个：10 + 1 = eleven；再加 -th 就从“十一”变为“第十一”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Count ten, with one left over: 10 + 1 = eleven; add -th to move from the quantity eleven to the position eleventh.

pronunciation.label: 美式教学读法
pronunciation.note: 常见读法是两个音节；拼写中的第一个 d 通常不发音。

forms: 单数 Wednesday；复数 Wednesdays 可指多个星期三。常见缩写 Wed.。
family: Wednesdays 是同一名词的复数；作时间副词时可表示每逢星期三。没有常用的派生词需要另外背。

morphology.text: Wednesday（星期三）+ -s（复数后缀）→ Wednesdays：多个星期三；也可用于表示每周三。

etymology.text: 名字来自古英语的“Woden 的一天”，Woden 是古代日耳曼神祇的名字，也与 Odin 相对应。可把它记成有古老名字的那一天。

usage_note: 星期名首字母必须大写。说某个星期三用 on Wednesday；next Wednesday、last Wednesday 前通常不用 on。

senses.meaning_zh: 星期三
senses.meaning_en: the day between Tuesday and Thursday
senses.english_definition: Wednesday is the day of the week after Tuesday and before Thursday.
senses.collocation_en: Wednesday morning; every Wednesday
senses.collocation_zh: 星期三上午；每周三
senses.sentence_en: The next meeting is on Wednesday.
senses.sentence_zh: 下次会议在星期三举行。

senses.meaning_en: on Wednesday, chiefly in American English
senses.english_definition: If something happens Wednesday, it happens on that day of the week.

senses.collocation_zh: 星期三到达；星期三上午离开
senses.sentence_en: We fly home Wednesday.
senses.sentence_zh: 我们星期三乘飞机回家。

etymology_story.zh: 源自古英语 Wōdnesdæg，意为“沃登之日”；沃登是与北欧神话中的奥丁相对应的日耳曼神祇。这一名称沿用了以神祇命名星期的传统，现代读音已不再逐一读出拼写中的所有辅音。
etymology_story.en: Wednesday comes from Old English Wōdnesdæg, meaning 'Woden’s day'; Woden is the Germanic deity corresponding to the Norse Odin. The name preserves the tradition of naming weekdays after deities, while its modern pronunciation no longer sounds every written consonant.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中通常将 Wednesday 作为整体词学习：词尾 day 表示“日”，但 Wednes- 不是能独立使用的现代词根。常见相关形式：Wednesdays（名词复数“多个星期三”，也可作副词表示“每逢星期三”）、Wednesday's（单数所有格）、Wednesdays'（复数所有格）；缩写为 Wed.。Wednesday morning 中的 Wednesday 是名词作前置修饰语。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, Wednesday is normally learned as a whole word: day remains recognizable, but Wednes- is not an independent modern root. Related forms are Wednesdays, a plural noun or an adverb meaning 'every Wednesday'; Wednesday's, the singular possessive; and Wednesdays', the plural possessive. The abbreviation is Wed. In Wednesday morning, Wednesday is an attributive noun.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 没有普通的完全同义词。Wed. 是书面缩写；hump day 是主要见于北美的非正式称呼，把星期三看作工作周的中点；midweek 指一周的中间时段，范围比星期三更宽。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: There is no ordinary exact synonym. Wed. is a written abbreviation; hump day is a chiefly North American informal name presenting Wednesday as the midpoint of the working week; midweek refers more broadly to the middle of the week.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 历史锚点：Woden + day → 沃登之日 → 星期三；读音抓住“Wenz-day”，不要逐字母拼读。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Historical anchor: Woden + day → Woden’s day → Wednesday. Remember the spoken shape 'Wenz-day' instead of sounding out every letter.

meaning: 休息充分的；精神恢复的

pronunciation.label: 美式教学读法
pronunciation.note: -ed 在 /t/ 后读 /ɪd/，全词有两个音节。

forms: 本课 rested 是形容词，比较可用 more rested、most rested。rested 也可作 rest 的过去式或过去分词。
family: rest n./v. 休息；resting、rests 是动词词形。restful adj. 让人放松的；restless adj. 坐立不安的；restfully、restlessly 是副词，restfulness、restlessness 是名词。

morphology.text: rest（休息）+ -ed（表示已完成的状态）→ rested：得到休息、恢复精神的。

etymology.text: rested 来自 rest 的 -ed 形式，后来也用作形容词描述休息后的状态。助记：先休息 rest，才会感到 rested。

usage_note: 常说 feel rested、look rested、well rested。I feel rested 描述状态；I rested yesterday 描述昨天休息过。

senses.pos: v. 动词（rest 的过去式和过去分词）
senses.meaning_zh: 结束举证或陈述；结束论证
senses.meaning_en: finished presenting evidence or an argument
senses.english_definition: If a lawyer rested their case, they finished presenting their evidence; in ordinary conversation, the expression can mean that an argument has been sufficiently proved.
senses.collocation_en: rested its case; the defense rested
senses.collocation_zh: 结束了举证；辩方结束了举证

senses.sentence_zh: 控方传唤最后一名证人后结束了举证。

etymology_story.zh: rested 由 rest 加 -ed 构成；表示“休息”的 rest 源自古英语 rest／ræst，意为“休息、安歇”。其过去分词进一步形成形容词，表示经过休息后恢复体力或精神的状态。
etymology_story.en: Rested is formed from rest with -ed; rest in the sense of repose goes back to Old English rest or ræst, meaning rest or a resting place. Its past participle also developed adjectival use for the refreshed state that follows rest.

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词公式：rest（休息；支撑）+ -ed → rested。作动词时，-ed 标记过去式或过去分词；作形容词时，表示休息后的状态；由于 rest 以 /t/ 结尾，-ed 读 /ɪd/。常见词族：rest、rests、resting、rested、restful（使人放松的）、restfully（安宁地）、restfulness（安宁）、restless（坐立不安的）、restlessly（不安地）、restlessness（躁动）、unrest（动荡）、well-rested（休息充分的）。
morphology_enriched.en: Formation: rest, meaning repose or support, + -ed → rested. As a verb, -ed marks the past tense or past participle; as an adjective, it describes the state following rest. Because rest ends in /t/, -ed is pronounced /ɪd/. Common family members include rest, rests, resting, rested, restful, restfully, restfulness, restless, restlessly, restlessness, unrest, and well-rested.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 形容词近义词：refreshed 强调疲劳消退后的清爽感，来源不限于睡眠；rejuvenated 强调活力明显恢复，语气更强；relaxed 强调身心放松，但不一定表示睡眠或休息充分。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: For the adjective, refreshed emphasizes renewed freshness, which may come from more than sleep; rejuvenated suggests a stronger renewal of energy; relaxed emphasizes freedom from tension without necessarily implying sufficient sleep or rest.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: rest 是“休息”，rested 是“休息过了”：人因此精神恢复，物体则可以稳稳搁在支撑面上。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Rest means taking a break; rested means the rest has happened. A person may feel restored, while an object may have been placed at rest on a support.

pronunciation.label: 美式教学读法

forms: 单数 Tuesday；复数 Tuesdays。缩写 Tue. 或 Tues.。
family: Tuesdays 是同一名词的复数，也可作时间副词表示每逢星期二；Tue.、Tues. 是缩写。

morphology.text: Tuesday（星期二）+ -s（复数后缀）→ Tuesdays：多个星期二；也可表示每周二。

etymology.text: 名字来自古英语的“Tiw 的一天”，Tiw 是古代日耳曼的战神。这个古老名字保留在今天的星期二里。

usage_note: 星期名首字母大写。on Tuesday 指某个星期二；next Tuesday、last Tuesday 前通常不用 on。

etymology_story.zh: 源自古英语 Tīwesdæg，意为“提乌之日”；提乌是与北欧神祇提尔相对应的日耳曼战神。这一名称以日耳曼神祇替代罗马战神马尔斯，沿用了拉丁语“战神之日”的命名模式。
etymology_story.en: Tuesday comes from Old English Tīwesdæg, meaning 'Tiw’s day'; Tiw is a Germanic war god corresponding to the Norse Tyr. The name follows the Latin pattern of 'Mars’s day', substituting a Germanic deity for the Roman war god.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中通常将 Tuesday 作为整体词学习：day 仍可识别为“日”，但 Tues- 不是能独立使用的现代词根。常见相关形式：Tuesdays（名词复数“多个星期二”，也可作副词表示“每逢星期二”）、Tuesday's（单数所有格）、Tuesdays'（复数所有格）；缩写为 Tue. 或 Tues.。Tuesday afternoon 中的 Tuesday 是名词作前置修饰语。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, Tuesday is normally learned as a whole word: day remains recognizable, but Tues- is not an independent modern root. Related forms are Tuesdays, a plural noun or an adverb meaning 'every Tuesday'; Tuesday's, the singular possessive; and Tuesdays', the plural possessive. Abbreviations include Tue. and Tues. In Tuesday afternoon, Tuesday is an attributive noun.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 没有普通的完全同义词。Tue. 和 Tues. 都是 Tuesday 的书面缩写，前者更短；the day after Monday 是明确的解释性说法，但不是另一个星期名称。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: There is no ordinary exact synonym. Tue. and Tues. are written abbreviations of Tuesday, with Tue. being shorter; the day after Monday is an explicit explanatory paraphrase rather than another weekday name.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 历史锚点：Tiw + day → 战神提乌之日 → 星期二。现代拼写保留古名，词尾 day 提示它是星期名称。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Historical anchor: Tiw + day → the war god Tiw’s day → Tuesday. The spelling preserves the old name, while day identifies it as a weekday.

etymology_story.zh: 由古英语 Þunresdæg 演变而来，原意为“雷神之日”，现代形式还受到古诺斯语 Þórsdagr 的影响。名称中的神祇是雷神索尔及其盎格鲁—撒克逊对应神祇，体现了以神祇命名星期的传统。
etymology_story.en: Thursday developed from Old English Þunresdæg, meaning 'the thunder god’s day', with its later form also influenced by Old Norse Þórsdagr. The deity is Thor and his Anglo-Saxon counterpart, preserving the tradition of naming weekdays after gods.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中通常将 Thursday 作为整体词学习：day 表示“日”，Thurs- 保留了古代神名的痕迹，但不是能独立使用的现代词根。常见相关形式：Thursdays（名词复数“多个星期四”，也可作副词表示“每逢星期四”）、Thursday's（单数所有格）、Thursdays'（复数所有格）；缩写包括 Thu.、Thur. 和 Thurs.。Thursday evening 中的 Thursday 是名词作前置修饰语。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, Thursday is normally learned as a whole word: day means a day, while Thurs- preserves part of an ancient divine name rather than functioning as an independent modern root. Related forms are Thursdays, a plural noun or an adverb meaning 'every Thursday'; Thursday's, the singular possessive; and Thursdays', the plural possessive. Abbreviations include Thu., Thur., and Thurs. In Thursday evening, Thursday is an attributive noun.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 没有普通的完全同义词。Thu. 和 Thurs. 都是 Thursday 的书面缩写，前者常用于空间有限的日历；the day before Friday 是明确的解释性说法，不是独立的星期名称。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: There is no ordinary exact synonym. Thu. and Thurs. are written abbreviations of Thursday, with Thu. useful in compact calendars; the day before Friday is an explicit explanatory paraphrase rather than an independent weekday name.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 历史锚点：Thor's day → 雷神索尔之日 → Thursday（星期四）。把 Thurs- 与 Thor 联系起来记忆，但不要把它当作现代规则构词。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Historical anchor: Thor’s day → the thunder god’s day → Thursday. Connect Thurs- with Thor as a memory aid, while recognizing that this is historical rather than a productive modern formation.

etymology_story.zh: boring 来自 bore 的 -ing 形式；表示“钻孔”的 bore 可追溯到古英语 borian。表示“使厌烦”的 bore 在十八世纪已有记录，但它与“钻孔”义之间的历史联系尚无定论，不能把二者的联想当作已证实的词源。
etymology_story.en: Boring is the -ing form of bore; the drilling verb goes back to Old English borian. Bore meaning 'make weary through lack of interest' is recorded from the eighteenth century, but its historical connection with drilling is uncertain and should not be presented as established fact.

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词公式：bore 去掉词尾不发音的 e + -ing → boring；可作现在分词、表示“令人厌烦”的形容词，以及表示钻孔过程或产物的名词。厌烦义常见词族：bore（使厌烦；无趣的人或事）、bores、bored（感到无聊的）、boring、boredom（无聊）、boringly（乏味地）、boringness（乏味，较少用）；钻孔义常见词族及复合词：bore、bored、boring、borer（钻孔工具或钻蛀虫）、borings（钻屑）、borehole（钻孔）。
morphology_enriched.en: Formation: remove the silent final e from bore and add -ing → boring. It functions as a present participle, an adjective meaning uninteresting, and a noun referring to the drilling process or its products. The boredom family includes bore, meaning to weary someone or an uninteresting person or thing; bores; bored; boring; boredom; boringly; and the less common boringness. The drilling family and compounds include bore, bored, boring, borer, borings, and borehole.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 形容词近义词：dull 强调缺乏趣味或生气；tedious 强调过程冗长、繁琐，令人厌烦；monotonous 强调缺少变化、反复单调。钻孔义须另行理解，不能用这些形容词替换。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: For the adjective, dull emphasizes a lack of interest or liveliness; tedious emphasizes wearying length or detail; monotonous emphasizes repetition and lack of variety. The drilling senses are separate and cannot be replaced by these adjectives.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: boring 让人无聊，bored 是人感到无聊；另记 bore a hole → boring a hole，表示钻孔。两组含义分开记。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Boring causes boredom; bored describes the person who feels it. Separately, bore a hole becomes boring a hole: keep the drilling meaning as its own memory link.

etymology_story.zh: goodbye 由16世纪的祝福语 God be with you（愿上帝与你同在）逐渐缩略演变而来。后来受 good day 等问候语影响，开头形成了 good 的拼写，原本的宗教祝福也逐渐成为普通告别语。
etymology_story.en: Goodbye developed from shortened forms of the sixteenth-century blessing God be with you. Expressions such as good day helped reshape its opening as good, while the religious blessing became an ordinary farewell.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 goodbye 是整体词，不能按 good + bye 来解释其历史构词；可作感叹词，也可转作名词。名词复数为 goodbye + -s → goodbyes；感叹词没有复数变化。常见异体拼写为 good-bye。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, goodbye functions as a whole word; good + bye does not explain its historical formation. It serves as both an interjection and a noun. The noun forms its plural with -s: goodbye → goodbyes; the interjection is invariable. Good-bye is a common spelling variant.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: bye 更随意，常用于熟人之间；farewell 更正式或庄重，常暗示较长时间的分别；see you 是口语告别语，通常带有以后再见的意味。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Bye is more casual and common between familiar people; farewell is more formal or solemn and often suggests a longer separation; see you is conversational and usually suggests meeting again.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 从“愿上帝与你同在”的临别祝福，记到今天的“再见”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Remember a parting blessing, God be with you, becoming today's goodbye.

etymology_story.zh: penny 来自古英语 penig、pening，最初指一种硬币，与德语 Pfennig 等日耳曼语词同源，其更早来源尚无定论。它后来成为英国货币单位的名称，并在北美英语中用于称呼一分硬币。
etymology_story.en: Penny comes from Old English penig or pening, a coin name related to German Pfennig and other Germanic forms; its deeper origin is uncertain. It became the name of a British monetary unit and was also adopted in North American English for a one-cent coin.

morphology_enriched.zh: penny 是现代英语中的基本词，词尾 -y 在这里不是可自由分析的后缀。指多枚硬币时，penny 去 y 加 -ies → pennies；表示英国货币总额时通常用不规则复数 pence，如 ten pence。常见词族及合成词：penniless（身无分文的）、pennilessness（身无分文）、pennyworth（少量；一便士所值之物）、penny-pincher（吝啬鬼）、penny-pinching（吝啬的；过分节省的）。
morphology_enriched.en: Penny is a base word in modern English; its final -y is not a freely separable suffix here. For individual coins, replace -y with -ies: penny → pennies. For a total amount of British money, the usual irregular plural is pence, as in ten pence. Common family members and compounds include penniless, pennilessness, pennyworth, penny-pincher, and penny-pinching.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: cent 表示美元等货币的百分之一这一单位，北美 penny 通常指相应的硬币；coin 是各种硬币的统称；copper 在英国口语中可指低面额的铜色硬币，并不专指一便士。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Cent names a monetary unit worth one hundredth of a dollar or certain other currencies, while North American penny usually names the corresponding coin. Coin is the general term for a piece of metal money. In informal British English, copper can mean a low-value copper-colored coin, not specifically a penny.

mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture a small coin: count the coins as pennies, but state British monetary amounts in pence.

usage_note: 常见结构是数词 + yards，如 five yards。一码等于三英尺，约 0.9144 米。此处说长度，不是房屋外的院子。

etymology_story.zh: 长度单位和帆桁义的 yard 来自古英语 gierd、gerd，意为“杆、棍”，后来分别发展为测量长度的单位和支撑船帆的横杆。庭院及作业场义则来自另一个古英语词 geard，意为“围起来的地方”，与 garden 在历史上同源。
etymology_story.en: Yard meaning a measure of length or a sail-supporting spar comes from Old English gierd or gerd, meaning a rod or stick. Yard meaning a courtyard or working area comes from a different Old English word, geard, meaning an enclosure, and is historically related to garden.

morphology_enriched.zh: yard + -s → yards，是名词规则复数；词尾 -s 在浊辅音 /d/ 后读 /z/。常见词族及合成词：yardage（以码计算的长度或数量）、yardstick（码尺；衡量标准）、yardarm（帆桁端）、backyard（后院）、courtyard（庭院）、schoolyard（校园空地）、farmyard（农家庭院）、shipyard（造船厂）、dockyard（船坞；船舶修造厂）、graveyard（墓地）、junkyard（废旧物品堆场）、scrapyard（废料场）。这些词分别属于“杆或长度”与“围合场地”两条词义支系。
morphology_enriched.en: Yard + -s → yards is a regular noun plural; the ending is pronounced /z/ after the voiced consonant /d/. Common family members and compounds include yardage, yardstick, yardarm, backyard, courtyard, schoolyard, farmyard, shipyard, dockyard, graveyard, junkyard, and scrapyard. These belong to the separate rod-or-length and enclosed-area branches.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: gardens 在英式英语中常对应美式英语中住宅园地义的 yards，但更突出种植和绿化；courtyards 通常指被建筑或围墙围住的庭院；depots 指货物或车辆集中存放、调度的场所，与作业场义部分重合。长度单位义没有可直接替换的严格同义词。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Gardens often corresponds to residential yards in British English, with more emphasis on planting and greenery. Courtyards are usually enclosed by buildings or walls. Depots are places for storing or dispatching goods or vehicles and overlap with some industrial uses of yards. The unit of length has no exact interchangeable synonym.

mnemonic_anchor.en: Keep two pictures: a rod gives the measure and the sail support; a fence gives the home yard and the working yard.
